returned_title: European Commission – CAP 2023–2027 Indicators and Reporting Methodology
justification: Official documentation and access information for CAP output, result, context, and impact indicators. Provides information on agricultural support measures, implementation years, and policy monitoring. Useful for correctly interpreting German agricultural policy datasets, including the distinction between claim years and financial years. This is primarily a methodological and data-access resource rather than a standalone dataset.

returned_title: European Commission – Agri-food Data Portal
justification: An official entry point for European agricultural and food-system datasets, including agricultural markets, food supply, agricultural income, EU financing, and CAP implementation. Germany-specific indicators can help researchers investigate the economic context of agricultural protests, food prices, agricultural production, and the relationship between farming policies and food-system outcomes.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – German Agricultural Statistics
justification: Germany's official statistical database provides downloadable agricultural statistics, including farm structures, agricultural production, land use, livestock, and economic indicators. Many statistical series cover the 2020s and offer geographic breakdowns. Useful for measuring structural changes in German agriculture and assessing economic pressures associated with agricultural protests. Data can be downloaded in CSV and spreadsheet formats.

returned_title: Destatis – Agricultural Census 2020 (Landwirtschaftszählung 2020)
justification: The official German Agricultural Census provides detailed information on agricultural enterprises, land use, livestock, farm structures, and agricultural employment in 2020. It offers an important baseline for examining structural conditions preceding the 2023–2024 agricultural protests. Regional statistics can support comparisons between Berlin, Brandenburg, and Germany as a whole.

returned_title: Destatis – GENESIS-Online Open Data and API
justification: An official interface for programmatically accessing German statistical datasets. Particularly useful for constructing longitudinal datasets covering agricultural production, food-related economic indicators, and regional agricultural structures during the 2020s. The REST API enables reproducible extraction of agricultural and related statistics for quantitative policy analysis.

returned_title: Robert Koch Institute – German Health Update (GEDA 2019/2020-EHIS)
justification: A nationally representative German health survey containing 22,708 observations and 310 variables, collected between 2019 and 2020. Relevant for studying nutrition-related health outcomes, overweight, obesity, and health inequalities. Scientific-use data include federal-state geographic information, enabling analysis of Berlin relative to Germany. Access to individual-level research data is subject to the institute's data-use procedures.

returned_title: Robert Koch Institute – Scientific Use Files for German Population Health Surveys
justification: An official catalog of scientific-use datasets from German population health surveys, including GEDA and other health-monitoring studies. Relevant variables can support research on dietary behavior, obesity, health inequalities, and nutrition-related policy outcomes. Geographic detail varies by dataset, and some surveys provide federal-state comparisons. This resource is especially useful for identifying appropriate microdata and access requirements.

returned_title: Robert Koch Institute – GEDA Health Monitoring Dataset Collection
justification: An official collection of German Health Update surveys with methodological documentation, variable inventories, and scientific-use data information. The 2019/2020 survey provides a baseline for evaluating nutrition-related population health during the early 2020s. Relevant for comparing nutrition-associated outcomes between Berlin and other federal states and assessing health inequalities related to food-policy objectives.

returned_title: Berlin Senate Department for Education – Open Education and School Data
justification: Berlin's official education open-data portal provides downloadable administrative datasets related to schools and education. It is a useful starting point for identifying data relevant to school nutrition policies, school infrastructure, and the implementation context of public school meal programs. However, the availability of direct indicators on school-meal participation, food quality, or nutrition-policy outcomes must be verified within the catalog.

returned_title: Berlin Steglitz-Zehlendorf – Public Health Monitoring Indicator 5.3.3: Nutrition
justification: A Berlin district-level public health monitoring resource addressing nutrition policy and institutional food standards. It documents the policy context for nutrition quality standards in daycare and school meals, including Berlin's use of German Nutrition Society standards. Particularly relevant to studying municipal nutrition-policy implementation, although it is an indicator and documentation resource rather than a comprehensive downloadable microdataset.

returned_title: Consumer Analysis 83/84 (Verbraucheranalyse 83/84) – GESIS
justification: Highly relevant dataset examining consumer behaviour in West Germany during 1982–1983. Covers purchasing habits, brand preferences, consumption of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, savings, financial products, insurance, travel, and shopping behaviour. Contains survey responses from 8,281 individuals aged 14 and older. Particularly useful for studying consumer preferences, purchasing decisions, and lifestyle patterns in early-1980s Germany.

returned_title: Income and Consumption Survey 1983 (Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe, EVS 1983) – German Federal Statistical Office
justification: Official German household survey providing detailed information about household income, expenditures, consumption patterns, and living conditions in 1983. Includes spending on food, clothing, housing, transportation, and other goods and services. Particularly valuable for quantitative analysis of household consumption, expenditure distribution, and socioeconomic differences in West Germany. Scientific-use microdata are available through the German Research Data Centre.

returned_title: Income and Consumption Survey 1988 (Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe, EVS 1988) – German Federal Statistical Office
justification: Official household expenditure survey covering West Germany in 1988. Provides information on household income, consumer spending, ownership of durable goods, savings, and living standards. Especially useful when combined with the 1983 survey to investigate changes in consumption patterns throughout the 1980s. The German Research Data Centre lists the 1988 microdata as available for scientific research.

returned_title: Household Panel 1984 (Haushaltspanel 1984) – GESIS
justification: Consumer survey conducted in January–February 1984, covering 7,346 respondents in West Germany. Focuses on household ownership, acquisition, and use of consumer electronics, including televisions, video recorders, radios, stereo systems, cassette players, cameras, and watches. Includes information on brands, purchase prices, purchasing locations, and product characteristics. Particularly useful for studying technology adoption, durable-goods consumption, and brand preferences during the 1980s.

returned_title: Percentages 4: Beverage Consumption 1987 (Prozente 4 – Getränkekonsum 1987) – GESIS
justification: Detailed consumer behaviour survey conducted between September 1986 and May 1987 among 6,016 adults in West Germany. Examines beverage consumption, brand awareness, purchasing preferences, drinking frequency, restaurant visits, dining expenditures, and health-conscious eating habits. Particularly valuable for research on food and beverage markets, consumer lifestyles, brand loyalty, and consumption preferences in late-1980s Germany.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2018 – DIW Berlin
justification: Major longitudinal household survey beginning in West Germany in 1984. Contains annual information on household income, economic circumstances, housing costs, employment, demographic characteristics, and living conditions. The 1984–1989 waves allow researchers to examine how changes in household income, employment, and socioeconomic status relate to consumption opportunities and economic behaviour. Particularly useful for longitudinal analysis of German households during the second half of the 1980s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 1980–1988 – GESIS
justification: Nationally representative social survey conducted in West Germany in 1980, 1982, 1984, 1986, and 1988. Includes information on household characteristics, income, occupational status, social attitudes, values, and living conditions. Although not primarily a consumer expenditure survey, ALLBUS is useful for investigating socioeconomic and cultural factors associated with consumer behaviour. The cumulative dataset supports comparisons across the 1980s.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for Germany: Application of Income and Supply, 1950–2013 – GESIS
justification: Historical statistical dataset containing 353 time series covering income allocation, consumption, savings, material living standards, and economic conditions in Germany between 1950 and 2013. Includes observations for the entire 1980s. Particularly valuable for studying long-term changes in consumption patterns, household purchasing power, and economic well-being. Suitable for historical trend analysis and comparison of consumer conditions across different decades.

returned_title: Eurobarometer 32 (October–November 1989) – GESIS
justification: Cross-national public opinion survey conducted in autumn 1989, including respondents from West Germany. Contains questions related to consumption, health, nutrition, smoking, alcohol, and social attitudes. Researchers can select German respondents to investigate consumer-related attitudes and behaviours at the end of the 1980s. Particularly useful for comparing West German consumer attitudes with those in other European countries.

returned_title: Income and Consumption Survey 1988: Food, Beverages and Tobacco – German Federal Statistical Office
justification: Specialized consumption data associated with the 1988 German Income and Consumption Survey, including detailed records concerning food, beverages, and tobacco products. Particularly useful for studying household food expenditure, consumption quantities, dietary purchasing patterns, and differences across socioeconomic groups. The Research Data Centre provides information about available EVS microdata and access arrangements.

returned_title: Consumer Analysis Series, 1980s (VerbraucherAnalyse) – GESIS Data Archive
justification: The GESIS Consumer Analysis collection includes historical consumer surveys archived under study numbers ZA1637–ZA1639. These studies examine consumer preferences, purchasing behaviour, product use, brand choices, financial services, and leisure consumption in West Germany during the 1980s. The series is particularly useful for exploring the relationship between demographic characteristics, lifestyle, and purchasing decisions. The linked record provides a verified entry point to the collection.

returned_title: City Development and Housing Milieu – Magdeburg 1986 (Stadtentwicklung und Wohnmilieu – Magdeburg 1986)
justification: Highly relevant dataset covering the German Democratic Republic in 1986. Examines housing conditions, neighborhood relationships, urban living environments, employment-related commuting, leisure activities, and cultural facilities in Magdeburg. Includes 74 variables concerning residential satisfaction, housing characteristics, transportation, leisure opportunities, community participation, and social relationships. Particularly valuable because it directly addresses Employment, Leisure, Community, urban and rural life, and Housing.

returned_title: Employment Survey for East Germany (DDR) 1989 (Beschäftigtenerhebung 1989)
justification: Comprehensive employment dataset covering approximately 8.5 million employees in the German Democratic Republic as of September 30, 1989. Contains detailed information about employment structures, occupations, industries, economic sectors, gender, age, regional employment distribution, and types of workplaces. Particularly useful for examining employment conditions and regional economic differences during the final years of the GDR. Access is restricted to authorized research and replication studies.

returned_title: Working and Living Conditions as Component of Way of Life 1980 (Arbeits- und Lebensbedingungen als Bestandteil der Lebensweise 1980)
justification: Survey conducted in the German Democratic Republic in 1980, focusing on working and living conditions among industrial employees and other occupational groups. Includes production workers, research and development personnel, and private and cooperative craftspeople. Relevant for studying employment, occupational experiences, and the relationship between working conditions and everyday life in socialist East Germany.

returned_title: Official Employment Statistics of the German Democratic Republic (Amtliche Statistik der Erwerbstätigkeit in der DDR)
justification: Historical statistical resource documenting employment in the German Democratic Republic, including information from the 1981 population and occupational census. Covers labor force composition, employment structures, economic sectors, and historical employment statistics. Particularly relevant for quantitative analysis of employment patterns during the 1980s and comparisons with earlier decades.

returned_title: Cultural and Social Living Conditions in the GDR 1988 (Erhebung zu kulturellen und sozialen Lebensbedingungen in der DDR 1988)
justification: Official GDR survey from 1988 documented by the GESIS German Microdata Lab. Relevant for investigating cultural participation, social living conditions, leisure, and everyday life during the late socialist period. Provides a potential source of microdata for examining social and cultural differences among East German residents. The linked institutional page documents the survey and related historical GDR datasets.

returned_title: Household Budget Statistics of the GDR 1988–1989 (Statistik des Haushaltsbudgets 1988/89)
justification: Historical household budget statistics collected in the German Democratic Republic during 1988–1989. Relevant to research on household economic circumstances, consumption, and material living standards. Potentially useful for analyzing the economic dimensions of housing and leisure, although the availability of specific expenditure variables should be verified through GESIS.

returned_title: Income Sample of Workers' and Employees' Households in the GDR 1988 (Einkommensstichprobe in Arbeiter- und Angestelltenhaushalten 1988)
justification: Official household income survey conducted in the GDR in 1988. Focuses on households of workers and salaried employees, making it relevant to employment, household economic conditions, and material living standards. Useful for investigating socioeconomic differences among households and their potential relationship to housing and leisure opportunities.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the German Democratic Republic 1989 (Statistisches Jahrbuch der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik 1989)
justification: Historical collection providing access to the GDR's official statistical yearbook for 1989. The yearbook series contains quantitative statistics on population, employment, economic activity, housing, social conditions, and other aspects of East German society. Particularly valuable for identifying aggregate indicators and investigating developments throughout the 1980s. The linked page provides access to historical statistical yearbook materials.

returned_title: Tourism Figures 1990 (Tourismus in Zahlen 1990)
justification: Official historical tourism statistics containing data relevant to travel and tourism involving the German Democratic Republic before reunification. Includes historical information on cross-border motor vehicle traffic between East and West Germany from 1960 to 1989. Useful for researching tourism-related mobility and travel patterns during the 1980s. The publication also covers broader German tourism statistics, so individual tables must be checked for GDR-specific coverage.

returned_title: Statistical Compass 1991 – Territory of the Former German Democratic Republic
justification: Official statistical publication containing retrospective indicators for the territory of the former GDR, including observations for 1980 and 1989. Provides historical statistical comparisons relevant to employment, population, living conditions, and socioeconomic development. Particularly useful for reconstructing changes during the 1980s and comparing East German conditions with those in West Germany.

returned_title: Living in the Former GDR – Retrospective Survey Data 2018
justification: Retrospective survey of former GDR residents concerning their experiences of life in East Germany. Includes historical information about occupational sectors and employment status in 1989. Relevant for studying social and economic conditions during the final years of the GDR. Unlike contemporary 1980s surveys, these data were collected in 2018 and therefore depend on respondents' recollections. Best suited as a supplementary historical source.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Relations and Support Systems – ISSP 2001
justification: This dataset is an exceptionally strong match for the query. It covers all 30 specified countries and regions, including Australia, Austria, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, Philippines, Poland, Russian Federation, Slovenia, Spain, South Africa, Switzerland, and the United States. Data were collected between January 2000 and April 2002. The dataset is explicitly classified under all three requested subject categories: Social behaviour and attitudes, SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS, and Family life and marriage. It examines family relationships, social networks, interpersonal contact, social support, relationships with parents and siblings, social trust, and participation in associations. This is the most directly relevant dataset for the requested geographic coverage, subject classifications, and time period.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles III – ISSP 2002
justification: This international survey examines family life, marriage, gender roles, household responsibilities, parenting, employment of married women, divorce, cohabitation, and attitudes toward children. Data collection occurred primarily between 2001 and 2004. It includes most of the requested countries, including Australia, Austria, Brazil, Chile, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Israel, Japan, Latvia, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Slovenia, Spain, Switzerland, and the United States. The dataset is particularly relevant to Family life and marriage and Social behaviour and attitudes. It also supports research on social stratification through demographic, occupational, educational, and household characteristics. Not every country specified in the query participated in this survey.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Role of Government IV – ISSP 2006
justification: This cross-national dataset examines social attitudes toward government responsibilities, redistribution, public expenditure, social welfare, civil liberties, political participation, and state intervention in economic and social affairs. Data were collected between 2005 and 2008. Participating countries include Australia, Canada, Chile, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Israel, Japan, Latvia, New Zealand, Norway, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Slovenia, South Africa, and Spain, among others. It is particularly useful for investigating Social behaviour and attitudes and SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS, including public perceptions of social welfare and inequality. Demographic variables also permit comparisons across family structures and socioeconomic groups.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Inequality IV – ISSP 2009
justification: The ISSP 2009 Social Inequality IV module provides internationally comparative survey data on perceptions of inequality, social mobility, occupational status, income differences, distributive justice, and attitudes toward socioeconomic hierarchies. It is directly relevant to SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS and Social behaviour and attitudes. Its demographic and household variables also support research on the relationship between family circumstances and socioeconomic position. The survey belongs to the requested 2000s period and provides a valuable complement to the 2001 Social Relations and Support Systems dataset. The linked official GESIS catalogue identifies the module and provides access to its documentation.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Religion III – ISSP 2008
justification: This international survey examines religious beliefs, religious participation, social values, moral attitudes, and the relationship between religion and society during the late 2000s. It is relevant to Social behaviour and attitudes, particularly attitudes toward religion, morality, and social institutions. It can also support research on SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS through comparisons across religious affiliations, educational categories, occupations, and demographic groups. Questions concerning social norms and family values provide additional relevance to Family life and marriage. The official ISSP data catalogue provides access to the 2008 Religion III module and its supporting documentation.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Leisure Time and Sports – ISSP 2007
justification: This cross-national survey investigates leisure activities, participation in sports, recreational preferences, social participation, and the relationship between leisure and other aspects of everyday life. It is relevant to Social behaviour and attitudes because it examines patterns of individual and collective social activity. It also supports research on SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS by enabling comparisons of leisure participation across educational, occupational, income, and demographic categories. Household and family characteristics offer opportunities to explore the relationship between family circumstances and leisure behaviour. The dataset falls within the requested 2000s period and is listed in the official ISSP data catalogue.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Networks – ISSP 2001
justification: This is the official GESIS documentation and dataset access page for the 2001 Social Relations and Support Systems survey, identified as archive study ZA3680. It is especially relevant because the survey investigates the structure and functioning of interpersonal networks, including relationships with parents, siblings, children, extended family members, friends, and other social contacts. It measures the frequency of interpersonal communication, geographical proximity to relatives, informal support systems, participation in social groups, and social trust. The survey covers the requested countries and regions and was conducted during the early 2000s. This record refers to the same underlying dataset as the first item but provides its official module-specific documentation and access point.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles – Cross-National Cumulative Dataset
justification: This cumulative international survey series combines comparable information from the 1988, 1994, 2002, 2012, and 2022 Family and Changing Gender Roles modules. The 2002 component is directly relevant to the requested period. The dataset series focuses on marriage, gender-role attitudes, household labour, women's employment, parenting, financial responsibilities, and changing family structures. It provides opportunities to investigate Social behaviour and attitudes, SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS, and Family life and marriage across multiple countries and survey periods. It is particularly valuable for researchers interested in comparing family attitudes during the 2000s with earlier or later observations. Country participation differs between survey waves.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Inequality – Cross-National Cumulative Dataset
justification: This cumulative ISSP dataset series integrates comparable survey information from the 1987, 1992, 1999, 2009, and 2019 Social Inequality modules. The 2009 wave is directly relevant to the requested decade. The series supports comparative research on subjective social status, socioeconomic inequality, perceptions of fairness, occupational prestige, social mobility, and attitudes toward income distribution. It is particularly well suited to SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS and Social behaviour and attitudes. Demographic variables, including household characteristics, permit investigation of associations between family background and perceived social position. The official GESIS cumulative-data catalogue identifies the dataset series and its constituent survey years.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Relations and Support Systems – ISSP 2001, GESIS Data Catalogue
justification: This is the official GESIS dataset landing page for the survey that most closely matches the query. It explicitly identifies the requested three subject classifications and documents the survey's international geographic coverage and collection period. The study provides respondent-level information on relationships with relatives, social contacts, family support, social networks, and community participation, along with demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Its coverage includes all 30 countries and regions specified in the query, making it especially suitable for comparative analysis of social behaviour, social stratification, and family relationships during the early 2000s. This is an alternative catalogue landing page for the dataset identified in the first item, rather than a separate survey.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 313: User Language Preferences Online (2011)
justification: Excellent match for both Media and Language and Linguistics. Conducted in January–February 2011, this dataset examines respondents' mother tongues, languages used to read and watch online content, languages used for online communication, and preferences for accessing websites in different languages. Its geographic coverage includes all 28 countries requested, including the United Kingdom. Available through the GESIS Data Archive as study ZA5473.

returned_title: Eurobarometer Media Use Trend Data (2010–2019)
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal data covering media consumption across European countries during the entire 2010s. Includes television viewing, radio listening, newspaper readership, internet use, and online social networking. The GESIS documentation identifies annual Eurobarometer waves from 2010 through 2019, enabling comparative research into media habits across the requested European countries. Particularly useful for investigating national differences in media consumption and communication.

returned_title: European Social Survey, Round 5 (2010)
justification: Cross-national survey dataset collected in 2010–2011, containing information about media exposure, internet use, social attitudes, and demographic characteristics. Relevant variables include television consumption, radio listening, newspaper readership, and personal internet use. Supports comparative research into media behavior and its relationship with social and cultural characteristics. Covers a subset of the requested European countries rather than all 28.

returned_title: Eurostat Adult Education Survey: Number of Foreign Languages Known (2011 and 2016)
justification: European statistical dataset measuring adults' self-reported knowledge of foreign languages. Includes observations from the 2011 and 2016 Adult Education Surveys, allowing comparisons of multilingualism during the 2010s. The 2016 survey provides statistics for the EU-28, including the United Kingdom. Particularly relevant to language proficiency, multilingualism, linguistic diversity, and cross-national differences in language knowledge.

returned_title: Eurostat: Pupils by Education Level and Modern Foreign Language Studied
justification: Harmonized European education statistics measuring foreign-language learning by education level and language studied. Includes observations from the 2010s and supports comparisons between European countries, including the requested EU member states and the United Kingdom where historical data are available. Useful for investigating foreign-language education, linguistic diversity, and the development of multilingual capabilities.

returned_title: Eurostat: Individuals Using the Internet for Participating in Social Networks
justification: European statistical data on individuals using the internet to participate in social networks. Includes observations from the 2010s, with country-level comparisons and demographic breakdowns. Relevant to digital media, online communication, and internet-mediated social interaction. The historical EU-28 series is particularly useful for comparing social networking behavior across the requested countries, including the United Kingdom.

returned_title: European Social Survey: Cross-National Survey Data, 2010–2018
justification: Official data portal for the European Social Survey, providing access to multiple survey rounds conducted during the 2010s, including 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018. Relevant topics include media use, internet access, social trust, national identity, and demographic characteristics. The surveys support analysis of communication behavior and cultural differences across participating European countries. Country participation varies by round, so the complete requested country list is not covered in every wave.

returned_title: GESIS Eurobarometer Data Service: Survey Data and Documentation (2010–2019)
justification: Official research-data access point for Eurobarometer surveys, including Standard, Special, and Flash Eurobarometer datasets collected during the 2010s. Relevant topics include media consumption, online communication, language preferences, multilingualism, and foreign-language proficiency. Many surveys cover all 28 requested countries, including the United Kingdom. Provides access to survey datasets, questionnaires, codebooks, and methodological documentation, making it valuable for identifying additional studies at the intersection of media and linguistics.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: A comprehensive dataset covering social behaviour, political attitudes, government satisfaction, social inequality, and demographic characteristics in Germany. Includes surveys conducted in 1990, 1991, 1992, 1994, 1996, and 1998. Particularly useful for examining changes in German society following reunification, including differences between East and West Germany.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1994
justification: A survey dataset examining political attitudes, electoral participation, voting behaviour, satisfaction with democracy, and perceptions of economic conditions in reunified Germany in 1994. Includes respondents from East and West Germany, making it particularly relevant for studying political integration and differences in political behaviour following reunification.

returned_title: International Social Justice Project 1991 and 1996 (ISJP)
justification: A comparative survey dataset covering Germany in 1991 and 1996. Examines attitudes toward social justice, income inequality, economic redistribution, occupational mobility, social stratification, and political values. Particularly relevant to equality, inequality, social exclusion, and political attitudes during Germany's post-reunification transition.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) 1992 – Social Inequality II
justification: An international survey dataset containing separate samples for East and West Germany in 1992. Covers perceptions of income inequality, fairness of earnings, social mobility, class differences, and the legitimacy of economic inequality. Especially useful for comparing attitudes toward inequality between eastern and western German populations shortly after reunification.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2024
justification: A longitudinal household panel dataset covering Germany throughout the 1990s. Contains information on household income, employment, education, living conditions, health, and social circumstances. Particularly valuable for examining economic inequality, poverty, social mobility, and differences between East and West Germany following reunification. The longitudinal design enables researchers to track changes in individuals and households across the decade.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) – Time-Series Dataset 1981–2022
justification: An international survey dataset covering social values, political attitudes, religious beliefs, interpersonal trust, democratic preferences, gender equality, and cultural change. Includes survey waves conducted during 1990–1992 and 1995–1998, allowing researchers to investigate relevant German observations from the 1990s and compare Germany with other countries.

returned_title: ALLBUScompact/GGSScompact 1998 – German General Social Survey
justification: A standardized survey dataset focused specifically on the German population in 1998. Contains measures of social attitudes, behaviour, social structure, and demographic characteristics. Suitable for investigating social and political attitudes and patterns of social differentiation toward the end of the 1990s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality Series, 1987–2019
justification: A collection of harmonized international surveys examining attitudes toward social inequality, income distribution, occupational opportunities, class conflict, and social mobility. Includes surveys from 1992 and 1999, with German participation enabling analysis of attitudes toward inequality during the 1990s. Particularly relevant for studying perceptions of fairness and social stratification.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Role of Government Series
justification: A comparative survey series investigating public attitudes toward government responsibilities, state intervention, welfare policies, public spending, and redistribution. Includes modules from 1990 and 1996. Relevant for researching political attitudes, government legitimacy, public policy preferences, and opinions about the state's role in addressing social and economic inequality. German observations can be selected where available.

returned_title: German Federal Election Studies – GESIS
justification: A collection of representative election surveys covering German federal elections, including those held in 1990, 1994, and 1998. Contains information on voting behaviour, party preferences, political participation, political attitudes, and evaluations of political institutions. Particularly useful for analysing democratic participation, party competition, and political changes following German reunification.

returned_title: Politbarometer – German Political Opinion Surveys
justification: A long-running collection of German political opinion surveys with coverage extending throughout the 1990s. Provides information on party preferences, political leaders, government evaluations, political issues, and public attitudes. Useful for tracking changes in political behaviour, public confidence in government, and political preferences during the reunification decade.

returned_title: GESIS German State Election Studies
justification: A collection of representative surveys associated with elections in German federal states, including elections held during the 1990s. Relevant for studying political participation, regional voting patterns, political preferences, and attitudes toward parties and government. Especially useful for comparing political behaviour across eastern and western German states following reunification.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Family and Changing Gender Roles
justification: A comparative survey series covering attitudes toward family structures, women's employment, gender roles, household responsibilities, and gender equality. Includes a 1994 survey wave, making it relevant to studying social attitudes and gender inequality during the 1990s. German data can be used to examine changing expectations about family and employment after reunification.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Religion Series
justification: An international survey series examining religious beliefs, religious participation, secularization, moral values, and relationships between religion and society. Includes surveys from 1991 and 1998. Relevant for investigating social attitudes, cultural differences, religious identification, and social change in Germany during the 1990s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Work Orientations Series
justification: A comparative survey series examining attitudes toward employment, job satisfaction, work values, occupational preferences, and employment conditions. Includes a 1997 wave. Relevant for studying social attitudes toward work, labour-market experiences, and employment-related inequality in Germany during the 1990s, particularly in the context of economic restructuring following reunification.

returned_title: GESIS Research Data Center Elections – German Election and Political Survey Data
justification: A research data collection providing access to German federal election studies, state election surveys, Politbarometer, and other political opinion surveys. Its historical holdings include studies from the 1990s, covering political attitudes, voting behaviour, political participation, and evaluations of democratic institutions. Useful as a central access point for identifying individual datasets from 1990, 1994, and 1998.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) – Wave 6 (2010–2014)
justification: One of the most relevant datasets for studying religion and values during the 2010s. Contains nationally representative surveys covering religious affiliation, religious beliefs, importance of religion, religious practices, tolerance, morality, gender roles, family values, social trust, and political attitudes. Includes Algeria (2014), Ghana (2012), Jordan (2014), Malaysia (2012), Nigeria (2012), and Singapore (2012). Particularly useful for cross-country comparisons.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) – Wave 7 (2017–2022)
justification: Provides individual-level survey data on religious identity, religiosity, spirituality, moral values, social attitudes, tolerance, gender equality, and political beliefs. Includes Indonesia (2018), alongside other relevant countries surveyed after 2019, such as Kenya, Mongolia, and Viet Nam. Researchers can select observations collected during the 2010s to maintain the requested timeframe.

returned_title: World Values Survey – Longitudinal Dataset (1981–2022)
justification: Combines multiple World Values Survey waves into a harmonized dataset suitable for studying changes in religious beliefs and societal values. Includes observations from the 2010–2014 and 2017–2022 waves. Useful for comparing religious commitment, traditional values, secularization, and social attitudes across countries and periods. Survey years can be filtered to 2010–2019.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Round 5 (2011–2013)
justification: Contains nationally representative public opinion surveys from African countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Nigeria. Relevant variables include religious affiliation, religious identification, interpersonal trust, democratic values, social tolerance, traditional authority, and attitudes toward political institutions. Provides an important early-2010s perspective on religion and societal values in sub-Saharan Africa.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Round 6 (2014–2015)
justification: Offers cross-national survey data on religious affiliation, social trust, political attitudes, democratic values, tolerance, and traditional leadership. Covers Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, and Algeria. Particularly valuable for examining relationships between religion, governance, and social values in the middle of the 2010s.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Round 7 (2016–2018)
justification: Provides nationally representative survey data for Ghana (2017), Kenya (2016), Malawi (2017), and Nigeria (2017), among other African countries. Includes religious affiliation and questions about social tolerance, community relationships, democratic attitudes, trust, and political participation. Useful for comparative research on religion and values during the latter half of the 2010s.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Country-Level Survey Datasets (2010s)
justification: Provides access to individual country survey datasets and supporting documentation. Especially relevant for Algeria, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Nigeria. Researchers can select country-specific surveys conducted during the 2010s and examine religious identification, social attitudes, tolerance, traditional beliefs, community participation, and political values.

returned_title: Arab Barometer – Wave II (2010–2011)
justification: Includes Algeria and Jordan and provides nationally representative public opinion data on religion, religious identity, democratic values, political Islam, gender attitudes, and social norms. Particularly useful for examining religious and cultural values at the beginning of the 2010s.

returned_title: Arab Barometer – Wave III (2012–2014)
justification: Covers Algeria and Jordan, with questions on religious practice, religious identity, the relationship between religion and politics, gender equality, social trust, and democratic attitudes. Useful for studying religious values and political-cultural change during the early and middle 2010s.

returned_title: Arab Barometer – Wave IV (2016–2017)
justification: Includes Algeria and Jordan. Provides survey information on religiosity, religious identity, religion in public life, social tolerance, gender norms, political attitudes, and institutional trust. Enables comparisons with earlier Arab Barometer waves to investigate changing religious and social values throughout the decade.

returned_title: Arab Barometer – Wave V (2018–2019)
justification: Contains nationally representative survey data from Algeria and Jordan, among other Middle Eastern and North African countries. Examines religious commitment, religious practice, social attitudes, gender norms, political participation, and views about religion's role in government. Particularly relevant for studying secularization, changing religiosity, and social values toward the end of the 2010s.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – International Religion Survey Datasets
justification: Provides survey datasets addressing religious beliefs, religious practices, religious identity, moral values, religious tolerance, and religion's relationship with politics and society. Includes international research conducted during the early 2010s, with relevant coverage of Muslim populations in countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Jordan, and Nigeria. Particularly valuable for studying religious attitudes across different cultural and geographic contexts.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – The World's Muslims: Unity and Diversity Survey (2011–2012)
justification: A multinational survey examining Muslim religious beliefs and practices, religious identity, interpretations of Islam, and attitudes toward religious traditions. Relevant to Indonesia, Malaysia, Jordan, and other countries with substantial Muslim populations. Particularly useful for comparing religious commitment, religious diversity, and the social significance of religion during the early 2010s.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – The World's Muslims: Religion, Politics and Society Survey (2011–2012)
justification: Contains survey responses concerning religious beliefs, moral attitudes, gender roles, family values, religious law, and relationships between religion and government. Includes Muslim-majority societies in Asia, the Middle East, and Africa, with relevant coverage of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Jordan. Particularly suitable for investigating how religious beliefs relate to social and political values.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – International Religious Restrictions Data
justification: Provides country-level indicators measuring government restrictions on religion and social hostilities involving religion. Covers all 14 requested countries, including Algeria, Ghana, Indonesia, Jordan, Kenya, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Mongolia, Malawi, Malaysia, Nigeria, Nepal, Singapore, and Viet Nam. Includes observations throughout the 2010s. Particularly useful for examining religious freedom, religious discrimination, and the broader institutional environment surrounding religion. Unlike public opinion surveys, these data measure country-level conditions rather than individual values.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – Global Attitudes Project Survey Datasets
justification: Provides international public opinion surveys covering social values, religious identification, attitudes toward other religious groups, morality, gender equality, and political culture. Selected surveys conducted during the 2010s include countries from Africa and Asia relevant to this query, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and Jordan. Country coverage and religion-related questions vary by survey year.

returned_title: Asian Barometer Survey – Waves 3 and 4 (2010–2016)
justification: A cross-national public opinion research program covering Asian societies. Its third and fourth survey waves fall within the 2010s and provide information relevant to social values, traditional beliefs, political culture, interpersonal trust, tolerance, and democratic attitudes. The broader survey program includes Indonesia, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Mongolia, Malaysia, Nepal, Singapore, and Viet Nam, although participation differs by wave. Particularly useful for studying how cultural traditions and social values relate to political attitudes across Asian countries.

returned_title: World Values Survey – Wave 6 Country Documentation (2010–2014)
justification: Provides country-level documentation, questionnaires, and survey information for the sixth World Values Survey wave. Relevant countries include Algeria, Ghana, Jordan, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Singapore. Especially useful for identifying exact survey questions about religious affiliation, importance of God, religious participation, religious tolerance, and moral values, as well as verifying country-specific survey dates and sampling methods.

returned_title: World Values Survey – Wave 7 Country Documentation (2017–2022)
justification: Provides country-specific documentation for surveys conducted between 2017 and 2022. Includes Indonesia (2018), with additional relevant country surveys conducted in the early 2020s. Useful for identifying religious values variables and checking which country surveys fall strictly within 2017–2019. Country documentation helps researchers avoid incorrectly treating post-2019 observations as data from the 2010s.

returned_title: Association of Religion Data Archives (ARDA) – World Values Survey 2010–2014
justification: Provides an alternative research archive for World Values Survey Wave 6 data and documentation. Relevant countries include Algeria, Ghana, Jordan, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Singapore. Particularly useful for researchers examining religious commitment, belief in God, religious attendance, religious identity, morality, social tolerance, and traditional values during 2010–2014.

returned_title: International Household Survey Network – World Values Survey 2010–2014, Wave 6
justification: A dataset catalog record documenting World Values Survey Wave 6, which covers approximately 60 countries and societies and more than 85,000 respondents. Includes Algeria, Ghana, Jordan, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Singapore. Useful for identifying comparable cross-national indicators of religion, beliefs, morality, family values, social trust, and attitudes toward cultural change.

returned_title: European Public Opinion and Foreign Policy: A Continuity Dataset (1952–1970)
justification: An exceptionally relevant dataset covering all four requested countries: France, Great Britain, Germany, and Italy. Contains survey responses from approximately 80,000 individuals collected between 1952 and 1970. Topics include international relations, Cold War politics, NATO, European integration, military security, nuclear disarmament, attitudes toward the United States and Soviet Union, and perceptions of war and peace. Particularly valuable for comparative analysis of public opinion during the 1960s.

returned_title: Correlates of War: Intergovernmental Organizations Dataset (1815–2014), Version 3
justification: Provides historical information about membership in international governmental organizations, covering all four countries during the 1960s. Suitable for investigating participation in international institutions, multilateral cooperation, international political integration, and diplomatic relationships. Includes country-level, organization-level, and country-pair observations. Records are available at five-year intervals through 1965 and annually thereafter.

returned_title: United Nations General Assembly Voting Data (1946–2026)
justification: Official United Nations dataset documenting General Assembly voting behavior from 1946 onward. Contains historical voting records for France, Great Britain, Italy, and both German states following their admission to the UN in 1973. Particularly useful for comparing the diplomatic positions of France, Great Britain, and Italy during the 1960s on international security, decolonization, disarmament, peace, and international cooperation. Germany's absence from UN membership during the 1960s is an important coverage limitation.

returned_title: Correlates of War: Formal Alliances Dataset (1816–2012), Version 4.1
justification: Documents formal interstate alliances, including defense pacts, neutrality agreements, non-aggression treaties, and ententes. Covers the 1960s and enables comparative analysis of the alliance relationships of France, Great Britain, West Germany, and Italy. Particularly relevant for studying NATO, Cold War security arrangements, collective defense, military cooperation, and the institutional structure of international security.

returned_title: Correlates of War: Militarized Interstate Disputes Dataset (1816–2014), Version 5.0
justification: Records international disputes involving threats, displays, or uses of military force between states. Covers the entire 1960s and allows researchers to identify incidents involving France, Great Britain, Germany, and Italy. Useful for examining Cold War confrontations, military crises, international tensions, conflict escalation, and the use of coercive diplomacy. Particularly valuable because it includes militarized disputes that did not escalate into full-scale wars.

returned_title: UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset (1946–2025)
justification: Internationally recognized dataset documenting state-based armed conflicts from 1946 onward. Covers the entire 1960s and supports investigation of armed conflicts involving the four requested countries, including their participation in conflicts outside Europe. Provides information about conflict participants, duration, incompatibilities, and intensity. Relevant for studying decolonization, military interventions, international security, and patterns of organized violence during the Cold War.

returned_title: Correlates of War: Interstate, Extrastate, and Intrastate War Datasets
justification: Provides historical records of wars involving states, including interstate wars, colonial and extrastate conflicts, and internal armed conflicts. Covers the 1960s and supports research into France's involvement in the Algerian War, Britain's postcolonial military engagements, and the broader security environment affecting Germany and Italy. Particularly useful for comparing different forms of warfare, identifying participants, and analyzing historical conflict patterns.

returned_title: Correlates of War: National Material Capabilities Dataset (1816–2022), Version 7.0
justification: Provides annual country-level measures of military expenditure, military personnel, industrial production, energy consumption, and population. Includes France, Great Britain, West Germany, East Germany, and Italy during the 1960s. Suitable for studying military capabilities, defense resources, power distribution, Cold War security competition, and national contributions to the international balance of power.

returned_title: Correlates of War: Militarized Interstate Dispute Locations Dataset (1816–2010)
justification: Provides geographical coordinates for militarized interstate disputes and associated incidents. Covers the 1960s and can be used alongside the main Militarized Interstate Disputes Dataset to investigate geographical patterns of military confrontations involving France, Great Britain, Germany, and Italy. Relevant for spatial analysis of international security, military crises, territorial disputes, and Cold War conflict geography.

returned_title: Attitudes Towards Europe (1962) – GESIS Study ZA0078
justification: Historical public opinion survey conducted in 1962 concerning European integration and attitudes toward international cooperation. Particularly relevant to France and West Germany and the development of European institutions during the early 1960s. Useful for examining perceptions of European political integration, international organizations, and interstate cooperation. Country coverage should be checked before making comparisons involving Great Britain and Italy.

returned_title: European Public Opinion and Foreign Policy: A Continuity Dataset (1952–1970) – Data in Brief
justification: Scholarly data publication describing a harmonized historical survey dataset covering France, Great Britain, Germany, and Italy. It includes repeated questions about international affairs, defense policy, European integration, NATO, the Cold War, disarmament, and peace. Particularly valuable for understanding the dataset's construction, methodological limitations, variable harmonization, and suitability for comparative analysis of the four countries during the 1960s. This publication documents the dataset listed first rather than providing a separate collection.

returned_title: Eurostat – Police-Recorded Offences by Offence Category (crim_off_cat)
justification: Highly relevant dataset covering police-recorded criminal offences, including homicide, assault, robbery, burglary, theft and other crime categories. Provides annual statistics from 2008 onward, including the 2010–2019 period, for the requested European countries. Particularly useful for comparing crime trends and law enforcement outcomes across countries. UK data are available through separate jurisdictions, including England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics
justification: Official European statistical collection covering crime, policing, criminal courts, prosecutions, convictions, prisons and criminal justice institutions. Includes historical datasets covering the 2010s for EU member states and the United Kingdom. Particularly suitable for comprehensive comparative research on law, crime and legal systems. The collection contains multiple datasets with different geographical and temporal coverage.

returned_title: Eurostat – Police-Recorded Offences by NUTS 3 Region (crim_gen_reg)
justification: Provides geographically disaggregated statistics on offences recorded by police, allowing comparisons between regions within European countries. Covers the 2010s, subject to country and offence availability. Particularly useful for examining regional crime patterns, differences in law enforcement activity and geographical inequalities in criminal activity.

returned_title: Eurostat – Prisoners by Offence Category and Sex (crim_pris_off)
justification: Official comparative dataset containing prisoner statistics by criminal offence category and sex. Covers 2008–2024, including the entire 2010s, although individual observations may be missing. Includes European countries such as Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, Poland, Sweden and the United Kingdom's constituent jurisdictions. Useful for researching imprisonment, sentencing outcomes and criminal justice systems.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice: Historical and Comparative Statistics
justification: Official entry point for European crime and criminal justice datasets, including police-recorded crimes, homicide, law enforcement personnel, court statistics and prison populations. Provides access to historical series covering the 2010s and earlier periods. Particularly valuable for longitudinal comparisons across the 28 countries specified in the query.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice: Statistical Metadata and Dataset Documentation
justification: Documents the Eurostat crime and criminal justice datasets, including offences, victims, suspects, convicted persons, police personnel, courts, prisons and human trafficking. Identifies datasets containing annual observations during 2010–2019. Especially useful for selecting comparable indicators and understanding differences in national criminal justice definitions. This is a metadata and dataset discovery resource rather than a standalone data table.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime, Violence or Vandalism in the Local Area (EU-SILC)
justification: Measures the percentage of people reporting crime, violence or vandalism as a problem in their residential area. Drawn from European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions. Relevant for studying perceived neighbourhood safety and crime-related living conditions across European countries during the 2010s. Complements police-recorded crime statistics by capturing residents' experiences and perceptions.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Trust in the Legal System, Police and International Institutions
justification: Comparative dataset based on the European Social Survey, containing measures of public trust in the legal system, police, national parliament, political parties, European Parliament and United Nations. Includes observations from the 2010s for participating European countries. Directly addresses law, legal institutions, law enforcement, international politics and international organisations. Country and survey-wave availability varies.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Trust in Others, Legal System and Politics: European Comparison
justification: Official Netherlands government data catalogue entry for a comparative European dataset measuring public confidence in police, legal institutions, politicians, political parties, the European Parliament and the United Nations. Contains historical observations relevant to the 2010s. Particularly suitable for analysing relationships between public confidence in domestic justice systems and attitudes toward international organisations.

returned_title: World Justice Project – Rule of Law Index: Current and Historical Data
justification: International comparative dataset containing historical Rule of Law Index scores from 2012 onward. Measures constraints on government powers, corruption, fundamental rights, public order and security, regulatory enforcement, civil justice and criminal justice. Includes numerous European countries and observations throughout the 2010s. Particularly valuable for measuring judicial effectiveness, rule of law and legal institutional quality. Coverage varies by year, and scores before 2015 require special caution when making longitudinal comparisons.

returned_title: World Justice Project – Rule of Law Index: Historical Editions, 2010–2019
justification: Archive of historical Rule of Law Index editions, including reports from 2010, 2011, 2012–2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017–2018 and 2019. Provides access to historical measurements of legal systems, criminal justice, government accountability, security and fundamental rights. Relevant for comparative research involving the requested European countries during the 2010s. Not every country appears in every edition.

returned_title: World Justice Project – Rule of Law Index: Country-Level Historical Rankings
justification: Interactive country-level data resource offering historical Rule of Law Index rankings from 2015 onward. Relevant indicators include criminal justice, civil justice, corruption, security, fundamental rights and constraints on government authority. Supports comparisons among European legal systems during the second half of the 2010s. Particularly useful for cross-country comparisons of justice system performance.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice: Statistical Collection Methodology
justification: Official methodological resource explaining the Eurostat and United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime joint collection of European criminal justice statistics, implemented from 2014. Describes data collected from police, prosecution services, courts and prison administrations. Useful for identifying the most appropriate datasets for European crime and law enforcement research during the 2010s and assessing international comparability. This is a supporting discovery and methodology resource.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics: European Statistical Metadata
justification: Comprehensive reference for identifying historical European datasets covering police activity, suspected offenders, prosecutions, convictions, prison populations and criminal justice personnel. Includes descriptions of annual data availability and the classifications used across participating European jurisdictions. Especially relevant for assembling a multi-country dataset covering Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Spain, Finland, France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Sweden, the United Kingdom, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia and Croatia.

returned_title: Czech National Election Study 2002 – Post-Election Survey
justification: A national post-election survey conducted following the 2002 Czech parliamentary elections. Relevant for studying voting behaviour, electoral participation, party preferences, political attitudes, and citizens' evaluations of political parties and institutions. The Czech National Election Study provides access information through its data catalogue.

returned_title: Czech National Election Study 2006 – Post-Election Survey
justification: A post-election survey examining Czech voters following the June 2006 parliamentary elections. Particularly useful for investigating electoral choices, political preferences, voting behaviour, and political attitudes during the 2000s. The dataset is archived by the Czech Social Science Data Archive.

returned_title: Comparative Study of Electoral Systems (CSES) – Module 2, 2001–2006
justification: An international comparative election dataset covering the period 2001–2006. It provides individual-level electoral survey data alongside information about political institutions and electoral systems. Its focus on democratic accountability and representation makes it useful for comparative research on political behaviour and elections. Researchers should consult the country coverage documentation to identify the relevant Czech observations.

returned_title: Comparative Study of Electoral Systems (CSES) – Module 3, 2006–2011
justification: A comparative dataset explicitly including the Czech Republic's 2006 and 2010 parliamentary elections. It combines individual post-election survey responses, electoral outcomes, and national political-system indicators. Particularly relevant for examining voter turnout, party choice, electoral accountability, and the relationship between political institutions and citizens' behaviour.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2009 – Voter Study
justification: A cross-national survey conducted following the 2009 European Parliament elections, including respondents from the Czech Republic. It contains information about electoral participation, party preferences, voting intentions, political attitudes, political knowledge, media consumption, and attitudes toward European integration. Particularly relevant for examining Czech electoral behaviour and political attitudes toward EU institutions in 2009.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Round 2, 2004
justification: A large-scale comparative social survey with confirmed Czech Republic fieldwork between October and December 2004. It contains measures of political interest, institutional trust, political participation, party preferences, ideological orientation, and attitudes toward democratic institutions. Suitable for analysing Czech political attitudes in comparison with other European countries.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Historical Rounds, 2002–2008
justification: A longitudinal comparative survey resource containing European Social Survey data from the 2000s. Relevant Czech survey rounds can be used to analyse political participation, institutional confidence, social trust, ideological identification, and democratic attitudes. The dataset is particularly useful for comparing political attitudes across countries and over time. Czech participation varies by survey round and should be checked before analysis.

returned_title: Party Preferences in the Czech Republic, 2001
justification: A dataset combining monthly Czech public opinion surveys conducted during 2001. It belongs to the Party Preferences Czech Republic series and provides information about citizens' political party preferences. Particularly useful for analysing changes in electoral support, political competition, and party identification before the 2002 parliamentary elections.

returned_title: Naše společnost 2002 – March (Our Society 2002)
justification: A Czech public opinion survey conducted in March 2002 by the Centre for Public Opinion Research (CVVM). It is part of the Our Society survey series, which regularly investigates citizens' political attitudes, evaluations of public institutions, electoral preferences, and social issues. Especially relevant for studying public opinion before the 2002 parliamentary elections.

returned_title: Naše společnost 2006 – December (Our Society 2006)
justification: A Czech public opinion dataset collected in December 2006 and archived by the Czech Social Science Data Archive. It belongs to the recurring Our Society survey programme, which covers political attitudes, government evaluations, party preferences, and citizens' perceptions of political institutions. Useful for investigating public opinion during the period following the 2006 Czech parliamentary elections.

returned_title: Czech Public Opinion Research – Our Society Survey Series
justification: A recurring Czech national public opinion survey programme containing datasets from the 2000s. Its political modules cover party identification, political orientation, political culture, confidence in political institutions, election-related opinions, government evaluations, and attitudes toward international organisations. Particularly valuable for studying changes in Czech political behaviour and attitudes throughout the decade. Individual survey waves are available through the Czech Social Science Data Archive.

returned_title: Czech Social Science Data Archive – Political and Electoral Survey Collections
justification: The national social science data archive provides access to Czech survey datasets, including historical public opinion research and election studies. Its collections contain relevant data on political attitudes, party preferences, electoral behaviour, and evaluations of government institutions during the 2000s. This is an archive landing page rather than a single dataset and is useful for locating additional Czech-specific studies.

returned_title: Czech National Election Studies – Historical Election Survey Collection
justification: A collection of Czech national election studies, including the 2002 and 2006 post-election surveys. It provides a starting point for obtaining individual-level data on electoral participation, party preferences, vote choice, and political attitudes. Particularly useful for comparative analyses of Czech parliamentary elections across the 2000s.

returned_title: European Election Study 2009 – GESIS Research Collection
justification: A research data collection focused on the 2009 European Parliament elections across EU member states, including the Czech Republic. It supports analysis of electoral participation, democratic representation, political communication, party competition, and attitudes toward European institutions. Particularly relevant for understanding how Czech citizens participated in European-level politics at the end of the 2000s.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2009 – CESSDA Data Catalogue
justification: A CESSDA catalogue record for the 2009 European Parliament Election Voter Study. The survey includes measures of trust in EU institutions, perceptions of political representation, electoral participation, and political party preferences. Czech observations can be extracted for country-specific analysis. This record provides an alternative discovery route for the European Parliament Election Study 2009.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: National Identity III - ISSP 2013 (Netherlands)
justification: The most directly relevant dataset, covering all four requested topics: cultural and national identity, minorities, international politics and organisations, and migration. Data were collected in the Netherlands between April and September 2014. The dataset contains 1,638 respondents and 130 variables. It examines national identity, national pride, attitudes toward immigrants, ethnic minorities, and international relations. Published by GESIS in 2017, it is particularly suitable for studying Dutch national identity and immigration attitudes during the 2010s.

returned_title: Survey Integratie Minderheden (SIM) 2015 - Survey on the Integration of Minorities
justification: A Dutch national survey conducted in 2015 examining the integration of ethnic minorities and people with migration backgrounds. It covers ethnic and religious identity, cultural values, discrimination, social participation, political participation, and relationships between minority and majority populations. Particularly useful for investigating cultural identity, minority integration, and migration in the Netherlands during the 2010s. The dataset is archived by DANS, with access restrictions.

returned_title: Dutch Parliamentary Election Study 2017 (DPES/NKO 2017)
justification: A national electoral survey conducted around the 2017 Dutch parliamentary election. It examines political preferences, voting behaviour, government evaluations, public policy priorities, and attitudes toward domestic and foreign policy. Relevant for studying how migration, national identity, and international political issues influence Dutch electoral behaviour. The dataset provides insights into political attitudes during a period when immigration and European integration were prominent electoral issues.

returned_title: Dutch Parliamentary Election Study 2017 - LISS Panel
justification: Survey data collected between March and July 2017 through the Longitudinal Internet Studies for the Social Sciences (LISS) panel. The study investigates Dutch political attitudes and electoral behaviour. It is useful for analysing relationships between political preferences, national identity, immigration attitudes, and international political issues. Its individual-level survey responses support research on differences in political attitudes across demographic groups.

returned_title: Dutch Parliamentary Election Studies 2012 - LISS Panel
justification: A dataset associated with the 2012 Dutch parliamentary election, offering evidence about political preferences and electoral behaviour in the early 2010s. Relevant for investigating public attitudes toward national politics, European integration, and migration-related political debates. Particularly useful when compared with the 2017 election study to identify changes in Dutch political attitudes over the decade.

returned_title: Statistics Netherlands (CBS): Population Development by Migration Background and Generation, 1996–2021
justification: An official statistical dataset from Statistics Netherlands covering population developments by migration background and generation. It includes the entire 2010–2019 period and provides demographic evidence about migration and population composition. Particularly useful for examining changes in the size and composition of migrant-background populations in the Netherlands. It can complement survey datasets by providing population-level context for research on minorities, migration, and national identity.

returned_title: Threatening Identities: Interaction and Conflict in the Multicultural Netherlands
justification: A LISS panel study examining perceptions of ethnic and cultural groups, intergroup relations, and identity-related tensions in Dutch society. Respondents from migrant-background and native Dutch populations were asked questions about different population groups. Although collected before the 2010s, it provides useful baseline evidence for studying cultural identity, ethnic minority relations, and multiculturalism in the Netherlands. It is most appropriate as a comparison dataset rather than a primary source for the 2010s.

returned_title: Election and Social Data of the Districts and Municipalities of the German Reich from 1920 to 1933 (Wahl- und Sozialdaten der Kreise und Gemeinden des Deutschen Reiches von 1920 bis 1933)
justification: A highly relevant historical dataset from the GESIS Data Archive covering the German Reich between 1920 and 1933. Includes Reichstag election results, population statistics, religious affiliations, occupational structures, and unemployment data at district and municipal levels. Particularly useful for examining political changes, the rise of the Nazi Party, and relationships between socioeconomic conditions and voting behavior during the Weimar Republic.

returned_title: German Weimar Republic Data, 1919–1933
justification: An extensive historical dataset provided by the Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR). Contains electoral and demographic information from 1919 to 1933, including Reichstag elections, presidential elections in 1925 and 1932, and national referendums. Also incorporates information from the 1925 German census, including religion, occupations, and urban populations. Suitable for historical research into political instability, electoral behavior, and the collapse of the Weimar Republic.

returned_title: Voters and Elections in the Weimar Republic, 1920–1933 (Wähler und Wahlen in der Weimarer Republik)
justification: A historical election dataset documenting voting patterns and political developments during the Weimar Republic. Includes Reichstag election results from 1920 to 1933, electoral district information, and statistical material on the social composition of voters. Particularly relevant for investigating the transformation of German politics during the 1920s and early 1930s, including the electoral rise of extremist political parties.

returned_title: Elections and Referendums in the Weimar Republic, 1919–1933 (Wahlen und Abstimmungen in der Weimarer Republik)
justification: A historical statistical collection associated with research by Jürgen W. Falter and colleagues. Provides detailed results of elections and referendums during the Weimar Republic, including electoral district data and social characteristics. Contains downloadable historical statistical files covering elections through March 1933. Useful for quantitative historical analysis of political polarization, geographical voting differences, and the development of support for National Socialism.

returned_title: Representatives in the Reichstag in the Weimar Republic, 1919–1933
justification: A GESIS historical dataset documenting 1,794 members of the Weimar National Assembly and Reichstag between 1919 and 1933. Relevant for studying the political elite, parliamentary representation, party affiliation, and institutional history of the German Reich. Particularly useful for examining changes in parliamentary composition during the economic and political crises of the late 1920s and early 1930s.

returned_title: Historical Statistics of Germany: National Economic Aggregates of the German Reich, 1925–1936
justification: A historical economic dataset covering the German Reich during 1925–1936. Contains national economic aggregates suitable for examining Germany's economic development during the late Weimar Republic and the early years of Nazi rule. Particularly useful for investigating economic fluctuations, the Great Depression, and the transition to the economic policies of National Socialist Germany.

returned_title: Basic Population Statistics in Germany, 1871–1939 (Grunddaten zur Bevölkerungsstatistik in Deutschland von 1871 bis 1939)
justification: A historical demographic data collection covering the German Reich, its constituent states, and Prussian provinces between 1871 and 1939. Provides systematically organized statistics on population size and demographic change. Particularly relevant for studying population developments during the 1920s and 1930s, including demographic changes during the Weimar Republic and the Nazi period. The extended coverage also allows comparisons with earlier decades of German history.

returned_title: Albrecht Ritschl's Historical Economic Datasets on Twentieth-Century Germany
justification: A collection of historical German economic statistics available through the University of Cambridge's Marshall Library resources.
