justification: United Nations statistical publication containing international reproductive health indicators, including reported legal abortions around 1990 and reproductive rights statistics. Includes German abortion statistics for 1992 and provides a framework for comparing reproductive health trends across countries. Useful as a supplementary source for examining Germany's reproductive health situation immediately after reunification. The figures are primarily national rather than specific to the former GDR.

returned_title: Politbarometer East 1991: Cumulated Dataset
justification: GESIS survey dataset examining public opinion in eastern Germany during 1991. Includes questions about abortion legislation and political representation of respondents' preferences concerning abortion regulation. Particularly relevant for understanding public attitudes toward reproductive rights in the former GDR following reunification. This dataset measures political attitudes rather than clinical reproductive health outcomes.

returned_title: Politbarometer East 1993: Cumulated Dataset
justification: Public opinion dataset covering eastern Germany in 1993, including questions about abortion regulation and political preferences. Useful for studying changing attitudes toward reproductive rights during the early post-reunification period. Can complement historical abortion statistics and fertility surveys by providing information about the political and social context surrounding reproductive healthcare.

returned_title: Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990)
justification: Highly relevant dataset collected in June 1990 in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Covers health-related information from individuals aged 14 and older. Provides a historical source for examining population health around German reunification. Archived by GESIS Data Archive.

returned_title: Partners III – Employed Persons 1990 (Partner III – Berufstätige 1990)
justification: Survey conducted in the GDR during the first half of 1990. Classified by GESIS under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions, particularly concerning HIV/AIDS, sexual behavior, reproductive health and disease-related awareness. Useful for researching public health attitudes and HIV/AIDS prevention in the final year of the GDR.

returned_title: Partners III – Apprentices 1990 (Partner III – Lehrlinge 1990)
justification: Survey conducted in the GDR in 1990 examining relationships, sexuality and sexual behavior among young people during the AIDS epidemic. Classified under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions. Relevant for investigating HIV/AIDS awareness and sexual health risks among young East Germans.

returned_title: Nuclear Energy and Environmental Consciousness 1990 (Kernenergie und Umweltbewusstsein 1990)
justification: Dataset based on a 1990 survey of 704 respondents across the five eastern German states. Classified by GESIS under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions. Includes perceptions of health risks, environmental hazards and nuclear energy. Particularly useful for studying perceived environmental health threats in the former GDR, although it does not primarily measure diagnosed diseases.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: Longitudinal collection of German population surveys, including eastern Germany beginning in 1991. Contains information about chronic illnesses, physical and psychological health, disabilities, healthcare utilization and HIV/AIDS awareness. The 1991–1998 survey waves are relevant for investigating disease-related conditions in the former GDR during the 1990s. Geographic identifiers enable East–West comparisons.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for the Federal Republic of Germany: Health
justification: Historical health-indicator dataset covering Germany from 1950 to 2013, including the 1990s. Includes causes of death, ongoing illnesses, disabilities, sickness absence, medical treatment and medication use. Useful for examining historical changes in health conditions around reunification, subject to the availability of separate eastern German observations.

returned_title: Life in Eastern Germany 1992 (Leben Ostdeutschland 1992)
justification: Population survey conducted in eastern Germany in 1992, shortly after the dissolution of the GDR. Includes questions concerning health, health-related lifestyles, social security and living conditions. Useful for contextualizing health and disease-related experiences during the transition from the GDR, although it is not primarily a clinical disease dataset.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS) and Historical German Health Surveys
justification: Official Robert Koch Institute study landing page providing information about German population health surveys and their historical comparisons. Particularly relevant because the earlier Health Survey East was conducted in 1991–1992 among residents of the former GDR, while the nationwide 1998 survey included eastern German participants. The surveys cover cardiovascular conditions, chronic diseases, health risk factors and healthcare utilization. Historical microdata access may require contacting the Robert Koch Institute.

returned_title: German Cancer Registry Data – Epidemiological Cancer Statistics
justification: Dataset resource describing cancer incidence, mortality, prevalence and survival statistics from the German Centre for Cancer Registry Data. Its geographic and disease-specific indicators are relevant for investigating cancer patterns in eastern Germany following reunification. The listed resource begins in 1999, so its direct coverage of the earlier 1990s and historical GDR territory is limited.

returned_title: GESIS Microcensus Trendfile
justification: Harmonized German microcensus data covering multiple decades, including 1991, 1993 and 1995–1999. Contains health-related variables and demographic information, potentially allowing analysis of residents of the former GDR after reunification. Useful for population-level studies of health inequalities and associated risk factors, although detailed disease-specific information may be limited.

returned_title: German Fertility and Family Survey 1992 (Deutscher Fertility and Family Survey 1992)
justification: Highly relevant dataset collected in 1992 examining family formation, fertility intentions, marriage, household composition, partnership histories, and attitudes toward children in reunified Germany. It provides an opportunity to investigate family life among people from the former German Democratic Republic (GDR) during the early post-reunification period. Particularly useful for studying changes in marriage, childbearing, and family structures following German reunification.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles II – ISSP 1994
justification: A 1994 international survey explicitly including separate samples from eastern Germany (1,097 respondents) and western Germany (2,324 respondents). It examines attitudes toward marriage, family responsibilities, gender roles, women's employment, childcare, and household arrangements. Particularly valuable for comparing family values inherited from the GDR with those prevalent in western Germany four years after reunification.

returned_title: Life in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: Directly relevant historical survey conducted in January 1990, during the final year of the German Democratic Republic. It investigates social conditions, personal relationships, partnerships, living arrangements, and life satisfaction among GDR residents. The geographical coverage includes the Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin districts. This dataset provides a particularly useful baseline for understanding family and partnership experiences immediately before reunification.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core): Longitudinal Household Data, 1984–2021
justification: A major longitudinal household survey that expanded to East Germany in 1990, allowing researchers to follow individuals and households from the former GDR throughout the 1990s. It contains information on marital status, household composition, partnerships, children, employment, income, and living conditions. Especially useful for investigating how reunification influenced family formation, marital stability, household economics, and gender roles over time.

returned_title: Population, Population Movement, Households and Families in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1947–1999
justification: Historical statistical dataset covering population development, demographic changes, private households, families, marital status, and numbers of children. Its geographical coverage includes the new eastern German federal states and East Berlin following reunification. The dataset is useful for examining demographic trends during the 1990s and comparing family structures in eastern and western Germany. It provides aggregate statistical evidence rather than individual-level interviews.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Family and Changing Gender Roles I–V Cumulation
justification: Harmonized dataset combining international surveys conducted in 1988, 1994, 2002, 2012, and 2022. The 1994 component includes respondents from former East Germany and examines marriage, cohabitation, divorce, household responsibilities, gender roles, and attitudes toward children. Useful for analyzing whether attitudes toward marriage and family associated with the GDR persisted or changed after reunification. Researchers can isolate the 1994 eastern German observations for analysis.

returned_title: Statistical Overviews of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone / GDR
justification: Historical statistical compilation focusing specifically on the Soviet occupation zone and the German Democratic Republic between 1945 and 1989. It provides contextual evidence on the development of social policies under the GDR, which is useful for investigating the institutional environment surrounding family life, childcare, and social protection. Although published after the 1990s, its historical coverage makes it relevant for understanding the family-policy structures inherited by eastern Germany at reunification.

returned_title: Bamberg Panel on Nonmarital Cohabitation (Bamberger NEL-Panel)
justification: Longitudinal study examining nonmarital partnerships, marriage, and changing attitudes toward family formation. Its survey waves include observations around 1990, making it potentially useful for understanding broader German changes in cohabitation and marriage during the reunification period. However, its geographical coverage and suitability for specifically studying former GDR residents require verification before use.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS)
justification: Major German social survey program that expanded its coverage to the former East Germany in 1991. Surveys conducted throughout the 1990s provide information on family-related attitudes, social values, household characteristics, and demographic circumstances. The program is particularly useful for comparing eastern and western German attitudes toward marriage, family responsibilities, and social change after reunification. The URL leads to the official GESIS survey data portal, where individual ALLBUS waves can be located.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2019
justification: One of the most comprehensive longitudinal datasets for studying social stratification in Germany during the 2010s. Contains annual individual- and household-level information on income, wealth-related indicators, education, employment, occupational status, migration background, household composition, and social mobility. Particularly suitable for examining economic inequality, class differences, intergenerational mobility, and changes in socioeconomic status between 2010 and 2019.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2018
justification: A nationally representative survey of Germany's adult population covering social structure, socioeconomic characteristics, attitudes, and social group differences. Includes information relevant to education, occupational position, income, social class, religion, and demographic characteristics. Useful for investigating social stratification and relationships between socioeconomic position and social attitudes in Germany in 2018.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2016
justification: Provides representative survey data on German society in 2016, including occupational categories, educational attainment, socioeconomic characteristics, political attitudes, and perceptions of different social groups. Relevant for investigating class structures, social divisions, educational inequalities, and differences between demographic groups.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2014
justification: Provides cross-sectional information on social structure and attitudes in Germany during 2014. Supports research on socioeconomic groupings, occupational stratification, education, social background, and demographic differences. Can be combined analytically with other ALLBUS survey waves to investigate changes in social stratification throughout the 2010s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2012
justification: Contains representative survey data on German social structure and attitudes in 2012. Relevant variables include education, employment, occupational classifications, demographic characteristics, and indicators of social position. Particularly useful for studying socioeconomic differentiation and social group membership during the early 2010s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: A harmonized cumulative dataset combining multiple ALLBUS survey waves, including those conducted during the 2010s. Enables longitudinal comparisons of repeated cross-sectional measures of occupational status, education, socioeconomic position, demographic characteristics, and social attitudes. Particularly valuable for identifying changes in class composition, social inequalities, and group differences across Germany between 2010 and 2019.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality V, 2019
justification: A survey specifically designed to investigate social inequality and stratification. Includes Germany alongside other participating countries. Covers perceived social class, socioeconomic inequalities, occupational status, social mobility, distributive justice, and attitudes toward income differences. Particularly relevant for examining subjective and objective dimensions of social stratification. Note that the German component of this ISSP 2019 module was collected in 2020, making it useful primarily as a measure of conditions and perceptions around the end of the 2010s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality I–V Cumulation, 1987–2019
justification: A harmonized international dataset combining five waves of the ISSP Social Inequality module. Includes observations for Germany and supports historical comparisons of perceived social class, occupational hierarchies, income inequality, social mobility, and attitudes toward redistribution. Particularly valuable for examining how German social stratification changed between earlier decades and the late 2010s.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 4: Grade 9, 2010
justification: A German longitudinal educational dataset following students who were in ninth grade in 2010. Includes information on parental socioeconomic background, educational pathways, school characteristics, migration background, and transitions into vocational training or higher education. Highly relevant for investigating educational stratification, intergenerational inequality, and the reproduction of social class during the 2010s.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 5: First-Year Students, 2010
justification: Tracks individuals entering German higher education in 2010. Contains information relevant to parental education, socioeconomic origins, educational trajectories, academic experiences, and transitions into employment. Useful for analyzing social inequalities in access to higher education, differences between socioeconomic groups, and educational mobility during the 2010s.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 6: Adults
justification: A longitudinal survey of adults in Germany with observations throughout the 2010s. Covers educational histories, employment trajectories, occupational mobility, lifelong learning, and socioeconomic background. Particularly valuable for understanding how education and labor-market experiences contribute to social stratification and mobility across different adult population groups.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Starting Cohort 2: Kindergarten, 2011
justification: A longitudinal study of children entering kindergarten in Germany in 2011. Includes information on family socioeconomic status, parental education, migration background, learning environments, and educational development. Suitable for examining how social inequalities emerge during childhood and how differences between socioeconomic and demographic groups influence educational opportunities.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam), 2008–2021
justification: A longitudinal German dataset covering family relationships, partnerships, household structures, and intergenerational relationships, with extensive observations during the 2010s. Includes demographic and socioeconomic characteristics that support analyses of social groupings by family status, generation, education, and social background. Particularly useful for studying relationships between family structures, socioeconomic inequality, and social mobility.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam) – Scientific Use Files, Waves 1–13
justification: Provides longitudinal information on partnership formation, family dynamics, fertility, intergenerational relationships, and socioeconomic characteristics in Germany. The waves covering 2010–2019 are useful for investigating demographic stratification, social differences in family formation, and relationships between educational attainment, employment, and household composition.

returned_title: German Student Social Survey – Pooled Data Set, 1982–2016
justification: A harmonized dataset covering the economic and social circumstances of students in German higher education, including survey waves from the 2010s. Contains information on parental socioeconomic background, educational origins, income, employment, housing, migration-related characteristics, and living conditions. Particularly relevant for analyzing educational stratification, social inequalities among university students, and differences in higher education participation across social groups.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Social Inequality Module Series
justification: Provides access to the ISSP surveys devoted specifically to social inequality, including the 2019 module and earlier comparative waves. Relevant for examining Germans' perceptions of class divisions, occupational prestige, income inequality, social mobility, and distributive justice. Particularly useful for researchers interested in subjective social stratification and comparative perspectives on Germany.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2020, EU Edition
justification: A longitudinal household panel covering the entire 2010–2019 period, with an additional observation year in 2020. Includes income, education, employment histories, household characteristics, health, and socioeconomic indicators. Well suited to studying poverty, income inequality, social class, migration-related inequalities, household stratification, and changes in socioeconomic status over the decade.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) – Combined Data Portfolio
justification: An official collection of German longitudinal educational datasets covering multiple age groups and educational stages during the 2010s. Enables comparisons of educational attainment, family background, migration background, employment transitions, and socioeconomic opportunities. Particularly useful for investigating educational inequality and intergenerational social stratification across different population cohorts. Scientific Use Files are available to researchers under data-use agreements.

returned_title: Second European Union Minorities and Discrimination Survey (EU-MIDIS II), 2016
justification: Conducted by the European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA), this survey collected data in 2015–2016 on ethnic minorities and people with immigrant backgrounds across Europe, including Germany. The German sample included 1,419 respondents of Turkish and Sub-Saharan African backgrounds. Topics include ethnic discrimination, employment, housing, education, harassment, hate crimes, police interactions, and social integration. Particularly relevant for studying minority experiences in Germany during the mid-2010s.

returned_title: EU-MIDIS II: Minorities and Discrimination Survey Data Explorer (2016)
justification: An interactive dataset provided by the EU Agency for Fundamental Rights. It allows researchers to examine survey findings on ethnic minorities and immigrants in Germany and compare them with other European countries. Data can be filtered by country, age, gender, and immigrant generation. Particularly useful for investigating discrimination, social inclusion, and differences between first- and second-generation immigrants in 2016.

returned_title: German Microcensus (Mikrozensus), 2010–2019
justification: Germany's official annual household survey provides extensive demographic and socioeconomic information. Data from 2010–2019 can be used to study populations with a migration background, including ethnic and national-origin minority groups. Variables cover citizenship, migration background, education, employment, household composition, and living conditions. Its large sample size makes it particularly valuable for analyzing relatively small minority populations and demographic changes throughout the 2010s. Access to detailed microdata is restricted.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2020
justification: A longitudinal household panel dataset administered by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin). It includes observations throughout the 2010s and contains information on migrants, refugees, and people with immigrant backgrounds. Relevant variables include employment, income, educational attainment, family structure, social participation, and subjective well-being. Specialized migration and refugee samples make it particularly useful for investigating socioeconomic inequalities and integration trajectories among minority populations.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 2018
justification: A nationally representative social survey administered through GESIS. The 2018 edition provides information on social attitudes, demographic characteristics, national identity, and aspects of immigration and social inequality. ALLBUS includes measures relevant to ethnocentrism, attitudes toward immigrants, and relationships between majority and minority populations. Useful for examining public perceptions of ethnic and religious minorities in Germany during the late 2010s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Historical and Cumulative Datasets
justification: GESIS provides access to repeated cross-sectional surveys covering Germany, including survey waves conducted during the 2010s. Topics include immigration, ethnocentrism, religious identity, attitudes toward foreigners, social distance, and minority integration. The cumulative datasets support comparisons across multiple years, making them especially useful for analyzing changes in German attitudes toward ethnic, national-origin, and religious minorities between 2010 and 2018.

returned_title: ALLBUS: Ethnocentrism, Minorities, and Migration Variables
justification: The ALLBUS thematic documentation identifies variables specifically addressing ethnocentrism, minorities, and migration. Measures include attitudes toward foreigners, perceptions of immigration, social distance from ethnic minorities, attitudes toward Islam, support for mosque construction, and perceptions of refugees. These variables can be located in relevant 2010s ALLBUS survey waves and used to investigate prejudice, religious tolerance, and minority acceptance in Germany.

returned_title: Second European Union Minorities and Discrimination Survey (EU-MIDIS II) – Survey Registry
justification: A research registry entry documenting the EU-MIDIS II survey conducted in 2016. It provides information about the survey's coverage, methodology, target populations, and data provider. The survey includes Germany and focuses on ethnic minorities and immigrants, particularly experiences of discrimination and social exclusion. Useful for identifying survey documentation and investigating access to research data suitable for secondary analysis.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP): Migration and Refugee Samples
justification: The SOEP includes specialized migration and refugee samples introduced and expanded during the 2010s. These samples provide detailed information about immigrant populations, including individuals arriving from European countries and refugees who entered Germany during the decade. Researchers can examine labor-market integration, educational attainment, economic inequality, household conditions, and social integration. Particularly useful for studying changes associated with Germany's 2015–2016 refugee arrivals.

returned_title: Eating Habits and Nutritional Status in Quedlinburg, 1985–1989: Part 3 – Dietary Habits of Pregnant Women
justification: Highly relevant primary dataset from the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Contains dietary information collected from pregnant women attending Quedlinburg District Hospital during the late 1980s. Records summarize individual meals and food consumption over a one-week period. Part of a ten-study research project examining nutrition among pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, and infants. Archived by GESIS and available for academic research.

returned_title: Eating Habits and Nutritional Status in Quedlinburg, 1985–1989: Part 2 – Sociological Survey of Non-Pregnant Women
justification: Primary research dataset examining nutritional status and eating habits among women aged 18–35 in the GDR. Data were collected during 1987–1988 from patients attending gynecological consultations in Quedlinburg. Particularly useful for studying dietary behavior, nutrition-related social factors, and differences between pregnant and non-pregnant women in East Germany.

returned_title: GDR Household Budget Statistics, 1988–1989 (Statistik des Haushaltsbudgets)
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for investigating food consumption in East Germany immediately before reunification. Contains household-level information on food expenditure, beverages, household income, and consumption of self-produced goods. Covers November 1988 through October 1989, with 40,594 household observations. Includes workers, agricultural cooperative members, and pensioners. Particularly valuable for analyzing food expenditure patterns, socioeconomic differences, and household consumption. Access to microdata is managed by GESIS.

returned_title: GDR Income Survey of Workers' and Employees' Households, 1988 (Einkommensstichprobe)
justification: Representative household survey conducted in the GDR in 1988, covering approximately 30,000 households and 80,000 individuals. Includes household income, demographic characteristics, and socioeconomic conditions. Although not a direct dietary intake survey, it provides valuable contextual data for investigating economic determinants of food consumption and nutritional inequalities in the GDR during the late 1980s.

returned_title: GDR Statistical Yearbook 1986 – Per Capita Consumption of Selected Foods and Beverages
justification: Historical statistical tables published by the GDR's official statistical administration. Includes annual per capita consumption figures for major food categories, including meat, fish, eggs, milk, cheese, butter, margarine, vegetables, potatoes, flour, and other products. Provides observations for 1980 and several subsequent years through 1985. Especially useful for reconstructing national dietary patterns and examining changes in food availability and consumption during the 1980s. Data are presented as historical tables rather than downloadable microdata.

returned_title: GDR Statistical Yearbook 1984 – Historical Food Consumption Statistics
justification: Official GDR statistical series containing per capita food consumption figures for 1980–1983 alongside earlier historical observations. Covers meat, dairy products, fats, cereals, vegetables, fruit, and other food categories. Useful for establishing baseline food consumption patterns in the early 1980s and comparing nutritional trends with later GDR statistical publications.

returned_title: Statistical Overview of Per Capita Consumption of Selected Food and Luxury Products in the GDR
justification: Historical statistical compilation presenting per capita consumption figures for selected foods and beverages in East Germany. Includes observations from the 1980s and facilitates comparisons across years. Relevant for reconstructing long-term patterns of food consumption, particularly meat, dairy products, and other staple foods. This is a secondary statistical compilation rather than an original survey dataset.

returned_title: Life in the GDR, 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: GESIS survey dataset collected in January 1990, during the final year of the German Democratic Republic. Covers living conditions, health, healthy lifestyles, consumer goods availability, economic conditions, and satisfaction with everyday life. Includes respondents from the Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin districts. Although dietary intake is not its primary focus, the survey provides important contextual information for examining nutrition-related living conditions during the transition from socialism to reunification.

returned_title: Statistical Overviews of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone and GDR
justification: Historical dataset compiled by André Steiner and archived by GESIS. Contains statistical time series describing socioeconomic conditions and social policy in East Germany, covering the GDR period and extending into the 1990s. Relevant for investigating the social and economic context of nutrition, including household living standards and welfare conditions. This is a supplementary source rather than a direct dietary consumption dataset.

returned_title: HISTAT: Basic Data on the Development of Health Conditions in Germany, 1816–2010
justification: Historical statistical dataset archived by GESIS, containing health indicators for Germany, including the former GDR. Its long chronological coverage allows comparisons between East Germany during the 1980s and unified Germany during the 1990s. Useful for studying population health outcomes potentially associated with nutritional conditions, although it does not directly measure individual food consumption.

returned_title: Nutrition Situation of the Population in the Former East Germany: Results of Household Budget Surveys in 1989
justification: Research publication reporting results from representative nutritional household surveys conducted in the GDR in 1989. Contains findings on energy intake, dietary fats, carbohydrates, proteins, and eating habits. Particularly relevant because it analyzes nutritional conditions immediately before reunification. Published in 1992, it provides a direct source of quantitative findings from historical nutrition surveys. The link leads to a research article presenting survey results, not a standalone downloadable dataset.

returned_title: Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990) – German Democratic Republic
justification: A highly relevant dataset specifically focused on health in the German Democratic Republic in 1990. Conducted by the Department of Medical Sociology at the Institute for Social Hygiene and Health Care Organization in Berlin, the survey covers individuals aged 14 and older. It provides valuable evidence about health and well-being during the GDR's final year. Available through the GESIS Data Archive.

returned_title: Life in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: A January 1990 survey examining living conditions, social security, health, healthy lifestyles, housing, and general life satisfaction in the GDR. Covers the districts of Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin. Particularly useful for investigating subjective well-being, perceived quality of life, and social conditions immediately before German reunification.

returned_title: HISTAT: Basic Data on the Development of Health Conditions in Germany, 1816–2010
justification: A historical statistical dataset containing official health indicators for Germany, including the German Democratic Republic. Covers mortality rates, age-specific mortality, life expectancy, and other indicators of population health. Its extensive historical coverage makes it particularly suitable for examining health developments throughout the 1980s and comparing the GDR with reunified Germany during the 1990s.

returned_title: Welfare Survey 1990 – East Germany (Wohlfahrtssurvey 1990 – Ost)
justification: A survey conducted between October and December 1990 examining objective living conditions and subjective quality of life among East Germans. Includes assessments of personal health, financial circumstances, employment, housing satisfaction, and general well-being. Contains 735 observations and 227 variables. Particularly relevant for studying health satisfaction and quality of life during the transition from socialism to reunification.

returned_title: Statistical Overview of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945: Soviet Occupation Zone / GDR
justification: A historical statistical compilation covering social policy in the Soviet occupation zone and the GDR, with observations extending from 1939 to 1996. Draws on official GDR health statistics, including annual publications from 1965 to 1988. Useful for researching health care provision, social protection, and the institutional conditions influencing population health during the 1980s.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core): Data 1984–2016
justification: A major longitudinal household survey covering health, employment, income, living conditions, and subjective well-being. Although the study began in West Germany in 1984, it expanded to the GDR in June 1990, before reunification. Particularly valuable for tracing changes in health satisfaction, economic security, and general well-being among former GDR residents throughout the 1990s.

returned_title: Life in East Germany 1993 (Leben Ostdeutschland 1993)
justification: A survey investigating social conditions and subjective well-being in eastern Germany three years after reunification. Includes questions about the importance of health, social security, employment, housing, healthy lifestyles, and overall life satisfaction. Particularly useful for comparing post-reunification experiences with the 1990 GDR survey and examining how political and economic transformation affected well-being.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for Germany: Health, 1950–2013
justification: A comprehensive collection of health-related social indicators compiled by GESIS. Includes life expectancy, causes of death, chronic illness, disability, medical treatment, medication use, health insurance, and occupational health. Contains 201 time series covering 1950–2013. Useful for analyzing long-term changes in population health during the 1980s and 1990s, although the geographic coverage of individual indicators must be checked before using them for GDR-specific comparisons.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS): Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: A cumulative social survey dataset containing information on general health, physical and mental well-being, chronic illnesses, medical consultations, disability, smoking, and subjective life satisfaction. East Germany was incorporated into ALLBUS after reunification, making observations from 1991 onward useful for investigating the health and well-being of former GDR residents. Earlier waves primarily represent West Germany and are more appropriate as comparison data.

returned_title: Human Mortality Database: East Germany
justification: An internationally recognized demographic database containing historical mortality and population statistics for East Germany. Provides data suitable for calculating and comparing life expectancy, death rates, and age-specific mortality trends during the 1980s and 1990s. Particularly valuable for examining changes in population health before and after reunification. Unlike household surveys, this source provides objective demographic measures rather than self-reported well-being.

returned_title: Everyday Problems of Young People in the GDR, 1988 (Alltagsprobleme Jugendlicher in der DDR 1988)
justification: A 1988 dataset produced by the Central Institute for Youth Research in Leipzig, investigating everyday problems experienced by young people in the GDR. Relevant to research on youth living conditions and psychosocial well-being during the late socialist period. It can complement population-wide health datasets by providing a youth-specific perspective, although the available variables should be checked for direct measures of health.

returned_title: Social Insurance, Personal Insurance, and Property Insurance in the Former GDR, 1950–1989
justification: A historical dataset covering insurance arrangements in the German Democratic Republic from 1950 to 1989. Relevant for studying the institutional and economic foundations of social protection and health-related security under socialism. Particularly useful for understanding the social welfare environment of the 1980s, although it does not directly measure individual physical or mental health.

returned_title: SOEP: Living in the Former GDR, 2018
justification: A supplementary SOEP dataset focused on individuals who lived in the former GDR before 1990 and were born before 1973. Although collected in 2018 rather than during the requested decades, it can support retrospective research on experiences of life in the GDR and their long-term relationships with well-being. It is most appropriate as a complementary source rather than a direct measure of health during the 1980s or 1990s.

returned_title: Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990) – German Democratic Republic
justification: Highly relevant dataset covering health conditions, chronic diseases, health behavior, medication, and medical treatment in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Data collection began in June 1990 and included individuals aged 14 and older. The dataset explicitly covers medication and treatment, making it one of the strongest matches for the query. Available through the GESIS Data Archive, with access conditions for academic research.

returned_title: Statistical Overviews of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945 – Soviet Occupation Zone and GDR (Statistische Übersichten zur Sozialpolitik in Deutschland seit 1945)
justification: Historical statistical dataset covering social policy and healthcare in the GDR from 1945 to 1989. It draws on official GDR healthcare statistics, including the annual publication 'Das Gesundheitswesen der DDR' for 1965–1988. Relevant for examining healthcare services, medical infrastructure, social insurance, and treatment provision throughout the 1980s.

returned_title: HISTAT – Basic Data on the Development of Health Conditions in Germany, 1816–2010
justification: Historical dataset compiled by Jürgen Sensch and published through GESIS. Includes official health statistics from the German Democratic Republic and reunified Germany. Covers mortality, life expectancy, health conditions, and the development of healthcare systems. Useful for analyzing health outcomes during the 1980s and comparing conditions before and after German reunification in 1990. Its focus is broader than medication and treatment specifically.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the German Democratic Republic 1990 – Healthcare and Social Services
justification: Primary statistical source containing annual healthcare data from the GDR, including detailed figures for 1980–1989. Particularly relevant because it provides annual expenditures on medicines, therapeutic aids, medical treatment, dental services, and inpatient and outpatient healthcare. Also includes statistics on completed therapeutic and preventive health treatments. One of the most directly relevant sources for quantitative analysis of medication and treatment during the 1980s.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the German Democratic Republic 1990 – Physicians, Dentists and Pharmacists
justification: Official statistical tables documenting the availability of physicians, dentists, and pharmacists in the GDR during 1980–1989. Includes annual figures and geographical breakdowns by administrative district. Useful for examining access to medical treatment, pharmaceutical services, and regional differences in healthcare provision during the final decade of the GDR.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the German Democratic Republic 1989 – Healthcare and Social Insurance Expenditure
justification: Official GDR statistical source presenting historical social insurance expenditure, including spending on medical treatment, medicines, therapeutic aids, and healthcare services. Provides quantitative evidence of healthcare financing and pharmaceutical expenditure during the 1980s. Particularly useful for studying medication costs and changes in treatment-related expenditure before reunification.

returned_title: Health and Social Insurance in the Former GDR, 1950–1989 (Personen-, Sach- und Sozialversicherung der ehemaligen DDR)
justification: GESIS historical statistical dataset covering insurance systems in the German Democratic Republic from 1950 to 1989. Relevant for researching the institutional and financial context of healthcare and social insurance during the 1980s. It can support analysis of how medical treatment was financed, although it is not specifically a dataset of medication prescriptions or individual treatments.

returned_title: Statistics on the History of Social Policy in Germany Since 1945 (Statistik zur Geschichte der Sozialpolitik in Deutschland seit 1945)
justification: Historical statistical collection incorporating primary information from GDR healthcare institutions, medical statistics, social insurance records, and official statistical reporting. Relevant for investigating healthcare provision, treatment infrastructure, and social policy in the 1980s. The source describes how GDR health statistics were collected from medical and social institutions, providing important methodological context for historical analysis.

returned_title: GDR Microdata – Household Budget Statistics 1988/1989
justification: GESIS provides information about representative microdata collected in the GDR during the late 1980s, including household budget statistics for 1988–1989. These data are potentially useful for investigating household consumption and expenditure related to healthcare, depending on the available expenditure categories. They provide socioeconomic context for studying access to medicines and treatment but are not specifically designed as medical datasets.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the German Democratic Republic 1989 – Medical Professionals and Pharmaceutical Workforce
justification: Official statistical source containing annual data on doctors, dentists, and pharmacists across the GDR, including the years 1980–1988. Provides numbers of healthcare professionals, population-to-provider ratios, and district-level statistics. Relevant for evaluating the availability of medical treatment and pharmaceutical services during the 1980s.

returned_title: DDR im Blick – Problems with Medical Supplies in the Healthcare System, 1989
justification: Digitized historical primary-source report from 1989 documenting shortages of medicines, medical supplies, and pharmaceutical products in the GDR healthcare system. Discusses supply problems affecting specific categories of medication, including cardiovascular medicines, and identifies factors contributing to shortages. Although it is an archival document rather than a structured statistical dataset, it provides valuable historical evidence about medication availability and treatment constraints during the late 1980s.

returned_title: AIDS in the Consciousness of the Population of the GDR 1989/1990 (AIDS im Bewusstsein der Bevölkerung der DDR 1990)
justification: Highly relevant GESIS dataset examining awareness, knowledge, and attitudes toward HIV/AIDS among the adult population of the German Democratic Republic. Data were collected between July and October 1990. The dataset directly matches the geographic, temporal, and subject requirements. It is available for academic research and teaching.

returned_title: National Cancer Registry of the German Democratic Republic (Nationales Krebsregister der DDR), 1954–1989
justification: Historical cancer registry containing approximately 1.8 million archived patient reports covering cancer diagnoses between 1954 and 1989. Records include cancer type, diagnosis, treatment, and disease progression. The registry provides extensive information on specific cancers during the 1980s in East Germany. Historical records are preserved by the German Federal Archives, with additional digitized registry information. Individual-level data are not necessarily publicly downloadable.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Reported Cases of Selected Notifiable Infectious Diseases in the Former GDR, Absolute Numbers (1950–1989)
justification: Historical statistical dataset containing 12 time series on selected notifiable infectious diseases in the former German Democratic Republic. Covers 1950–1989, including the entire 1980s. Particularly useful for examining disease incidence, infectious disease trends, and epidemiological patterns. Available through the Historical Statistics database (table C.01c).

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Reported Cases of Selected Notifiable Infectious Diseases in the Former GDR per 100,000 Inhabitants (1950–1989)
justification: Dataset providing 12 historical time series of infectious disease incidence rates per 100,000 inhabitants in East Germany. Includes observations from the 1980s and enables population-adjusted comparisons of infectious disease frequency. Particularly relevant for epidemiological research investigating specific communicable diseases. Listed as table C.01d.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Deaths by Selected Causes of Death in the Former GDR (1947–1989)
justification: Historical mortality dataset containing 22 time series categorized by selected causes of death in the former German Democratic Republic. Covers the 1980s and allows researchers to investigate mortality associated with specific diseases and medical conditions. Useful for analyzing historical patterns of disease-related mortality before German reunification. Available as table C.02c.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Cause-Specific Mortality by Sex in the Former GDR per 100,000 Inhabitants (1947–1989)
justification: Dataset containing 23 historical time series on mortality from selected causes of death, differentiated by sex and standardized per 100,000 inhabitants. Includes the 1980s in the German Democratic Republic. Particularly valuable for studying sex-specific differences in mortality associated with particular diseases and disorders. Listed as table C.03c.

returned_title: Statistics of Notifiable Communicable Diseases: From the Beginning of Records to December 31, 1989 (Statistik meldepflichtiger übertragbarer Krankheiten)
justification: Historical epidemiological statistics published by the Robert Koch Institute, incorporating infectious disease records from the former German Democratic Republic through December 1989. The publication compiles and contextualizes official statistics on notifiable communicable diseases. Particularly relevant for investigating infectious disease occurrence and historical surveillance during the 1980s. This is a statistical report containing historical data rather than a standalone machine-readable dataset.

returned_title: Statistisches Jahrbuch der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik 1989: Reported Infectious Diseases
justification: Official historical statistical table documenting annual reported cases of infectious diseases in the German Democratic Republic, including observations from 1980 through 1988. Covers tuberculosis, measles, diphtheria, scarlet fever, poliomyelitis, meningitis, hepatitis, salmonella poisoning, typhoid, and other communicable diseases. Includes absolute case counts and population-based rates. Highly relevant for research on specific infectious diseases in East Germany during the 1980s.

returned_title: Statistisches Jahrbuch der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik 1989: Deaths by Cause, Sex, and Age Group
justification: Official GDR mortality statistics presenting deaths categorized by specific diseases, sex, and age group for 1987. Includes malignant neoplasms, diabetes mellitus, ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, hypertension, pneumonia, asthma, chronic liver disease, tuberculosis, and other conditions. Provides disease-specific mortality counts with ICD classifications. Particularly useful for detailed analysis of disease-related mortality in East Germany during the late 1980s.

returned_title: Statistisches Jahrbuch der Deutschen Demokratischen Republik 1984: Disease-Specific Causes of Death
justification: Historical official statistics containing mortality information for specific diseases and medical conditions in the German Democratic Republic. Includes tuberculosis, malignant neoplasms, diabetes mellitus, circulatory diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, pneumonia, gastrointestinal ulcers, and other causes of death. Includes observations from 1980 and provides a useful source for examining disease-specific mortality trends in the early 1980s.

returned_title: Historical Cancer Registry Data of East Germany, 1961–2022
justification: Digitized historical cancer registry information covering eastern German states from 1961 through 2022, including the 1980s and 1990s. Originating from the GDR National Cancer Registry and subsequent regional cancer registration systems, these records enable investigation of cancer occurrence across the transition from socialism to reunification. The data are especially relevant for longitudinal studies of specific cancers. The linked archival description confirms the existence of the digitized records but does not establish unrestricted public access.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: Infant Mortality in East and West Germany (1946–2010)
justification: Historical demographic dataset presenting infant mortality trends in East and West Germany from 1946 to 2010, covering both the 1980s and 1990s. Useful for researching infant health outcomes and mortality differences before and after German reunification. Although not organized by individual diseases, the data provide relevant contextual evidence for research on neonatal and infant medical conditions. Available as table B.03.

returned_title: Destatis – Persons Engaged in Economic Activity in Germany (1991–2025)
justification: Official employment statistics from Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis). Provides annual employment figures covering the entire 2000–2009 period, including the number of employed persons residing and working in Germany. Particularly useful for analyzing national employment trends, employment growth, and the effects of the 2008–2009 financial crisis.

returned_title: Eurostat – Employment and Labour Force by Sex and Age (Annual Data)
justification: Official Eurostat dataset containing annual employment and labour force indicators for Germany and other European countries. Includes observations during the 2000s, with available data beginning in 2003. Allows analysis of employment rates by gender and age group, making it useful for studying demographic differences and comparing Germany with other European economies.

returned_title: Eurostat – Employment and Labour Force by Sex and Age (Quarterly Data)
justification: Quarterly labour market dataset from Eurostat covering Germany from 2003 onward. Provides employment indicators disaggregated by age and gender. Particularly useful for examining short-term employment fluctuations, seasonal patterns, and changes surrounding the 2008 financial crisis.

returned_title: Destatis GENESIS-Online – Population, Employment, Unemployment and Labour Force by Age Group
justification: Historical dataset from Germany's official statistical database, GENESIS-Online. Includes employment, unemployment, economically active and inactive populations, with observations covering 2000–2009. Useful for examining demographic patterns in employment and changes in labour force participation during the 2000s.

returned_title: OECD Employment Database
justification: Comprehensive international employment database maintained by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). Contains long-term historical employment statistics for Germany, including indicators relevant to the 2000s. Provides employment rates, labour force statistics, unemployment indicators, and breakdowns by demographic characteristics and job types. Particularly suitable for international comparisons and longitudinal economic research.

returned_title: IAB – Sample of Integrated Labour Market Biographies (SIAB)
justification: Detailed administrative microdata from Germany's Institute for Employment Research (IAB). The dataset contains a 2% random sample of individuals recorded in German employment administration systems. Employment histories extend back to 1975 for relevant West German records, with coverage of East Germany beginning later. Includes employment spells, marginal employment, unemployment benefit receipt, and participation in labour market programmes. Particularly valuable for studying individual employment trajectories, job mobility, and labour market reforms during 2000–2009. Access to detailed individual-level data is restricted.

returned_title: IAB – Sample of Integrated Labour Market Biographies (SIAB) 1975–2008
justification: Historical version of the German administrative employment dataset covering 1975–2008. Provides individual-level employment histories and labour market information, making it directly relevant to research on German employment during most of the 2000s. Useful for investigating employment stability, transitions between jobs, and labour market developments associated with the Hartz reforms. The linked publication documents this historical dataset.

returned_title: IAB Research Data Centre – Archived German Labour Market Datasets
justification: Official archive of historical labour market research datasets maintained by the Institute for Employment Research. Includes earlier versions of the IAB Employment Samples, Integrated Employment Biographies, Establishment History Panel, and other employment-related datasets. Several archived datasets cover the 2000–2009 period and support research on employment relationships, establishments, unemployment, and labour market policy. Particularly useful for researchers seeking historical dataset versions.

returned_title: Destatis – Population, Employed Persons, Unemployed Persons and Labour Force by Gender and Age
justification: Official German statistical dataset catalogued through the European Data Portal. Contains population and labour market measures, including employed persons, unemployed persons, economically active persons, and economically inactive persons, disaggregated by gender and age. Relevant for examining employment patterns in Germany during the 2000s. Historical availability should be checked in the underlying GENESIS table.

returned_title: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) – Employment-to-Population Rate for Germany
justification: Historical German employment-to-population ratio series distributed by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis using OECD data. Contains quarterly observations spanning the 2000s, including 2000–2009. Useful for time-series analysis of employment trends and assessing the relationship between employment and population changes during the decade.

returned_title: Eurostat – Employment and Labour Force by Sex and Age (European Data Portal)
justification: European Data Portal catalogue entry for Eurostat's annual employment and labour force dataset. Covers Germany and other European countries, with temporal coverage beginning in 2003. Includes employment indicators by age and gender. Useful for identifying the dataset's metadata, geographic coverage, and official source before conducting comparative research on employment trends during 2003–2009.

returned_title: German Management and Organizational Practices (GMOP) Survey – 2008 and 2013
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for studying business management and organisational practices in Germany. Contains establishment-level information for 1,927 German establishments, covering management practices in 2008 and 2013. Variables include performance monitoring, target setting, employee incentives, work-family balance, workplace health measures, sales, exports and innovation. Particularly valuable for analysing management structures and their relationship with business performance during the late 2000s. The dataset is restricted to replication studies, with access managed by the IAB Research Data Centre.

returned_title: IAB Establishment Panel (IAB-Betriebspanel) – 1993–2019
justification: A comprehensive annual longitudinal survey of German establishments, covering the entire 2000–2009 period. Includes information on employment structures, personnel management, organisational practices, recruitment, training, industrial relations, investment and business development. Covers establishments across different industries and regions of Germany. Particularly useful for examining changes in management strategies, workforce organisation and employment policies throughout the 2000s. Research access is available through the IAB Research Data Centre.

returned_title: Mannheim Enterprise Panel (MUP) – German Firm-Level Longitudinal Data
justification: A large longitudinal database maintained by the ZEW research institute since 1992, covering more than nine million German companies. Contains information on business formation, closure, growth, employment, sales, industry classifications, legal structures, ownership and financial characteristics. The dataset covers the entire 2000s and is particularly suitable for investigating enterprise organisation, ownership structures, industrial development, firm survival and business restructuring in Germany.

returned_title: Mannheim Innovation Panel (MIP) – Innovation Activities of Enterprises in Germany
justification: A longitudinal survey of innovation activities among German enterprises, conducted by ZEW as Germany's contribution to the European Community Innovation Survey. Includes observations from the 2000s and information relevant to innovation management, organisational innovation, technological development, research and development, innovation expenditure and business performance. Particularly useful for studying how German industrial firms adapted their management and organisational strategies to technological and competitive changes during the decade.

returned_title: ZEW ICT Survey – Diffusion and Use of Information and Communication Technologies, 2002–2015
justification: A representative firm-level survey examining technology adoption and organisational transformation in German businesses. Relevant survey waves include 2002, 2004 and 2007. Approximately 4,500 firms from manufacturing and selected service industries participated in each wave. The data include information on ICT adoption, organisational changes, workplace practices, employee characteristics, training and innovation. Especially valuable for studying how digital technologies influenced management structures, workplace organisation and productivity in Germany during the 2000s.

returned_title: ifo Business Survey – German Industrial Enterprises
justification: A long-running collection of business survey microdata provided through the LMU-ifo Economics & Business Data Center. The industrial business survey includes historical observations extending across the entire 2000–2009 period. It provides firm-level information on business conditions, production expectations, capacity utilisation, employment expectations and other indicators of industrial activity. Useful for analysing industrial management decisions, business planning and responses to economic fluctuations, including the 2008–2009 financial crisis. Access to confidential microdata is restricted.

returned_title: ifo Investment Survey – German Manufacturing Industry
justification: An established survey of investment activities among German industrial enterprises, with historical coverage extending well before the 2000s. Provides information relevant to investment planning, capital expenditure, business expectations and industrial development. Particularly suitable for investigating investment management, strategic resource allocation and capital investment decisions by German manufacturing businesses during 2000–2009. The ifo Economics & Business Data Center provides information about accessing the underlying microdata.

returned_title: Linked Employer-Employee Data from the IAB (LIAB)
justification: A longitudinal dataset linking information from the IAB Establishment Panel with administrative employment records. Historical versions include observations from the 2000s. The data allow researchers to examine relationships between establishment characteristics, personnel management, workforce composition, wages and employee mobility. Particularly relevant for investigating human resource management, labour organisation, workplace restructuring and the relationship between management practices and employment outcomes in German establishments. Access is subject to research data protection requirements.

returned_title: ZEW Quarterly Business Survey Among Service Providers of the Information Society – 2002–2011
justification: A quarterly firm-level survey conducted between 2002 and 2011, covering approximately 1,000 German companies in ICT-intensive service industries. Contains information on business development, economic expectations, investment in information technologies, employment, employee qualifications, training and innovation. Useful for examining management strategies, organisational adaptation, workforce development and business performance in Germany's technology-oriented service sector throughout most of the 2000s.

returned_title: ifo Innovation Survey – German Enterprises
justification: A historical survey series covering innovation activities among German businesses, including observations from the 2000s. Relevant for investigating innovation management, technological development and firms' strategic responses to changing market conditions. It can complement the Mannheim Innovation Panel by providing an additional source of enterprise-level innovation information. The ifo Economics & Business Data Center catalog provides dataset descriptions and access arrangements.

returned_title: ZEW ICT and Workplace Reorganisation Research Data
justification: A research project using German firm-level survey information to examine the relationship between information technology, workplace reorganisation and business productivity. Particularly relevant to organisational changes such as flatter management hierarchies, increased teamwork and changes in workplace structures. The underlying research relates to organisational transformation around the early 2000s. This is a research-project landing page rather than a separate public dataset download; it is useful for identifying relevant ZEW survey data and associated research.

returned_title: ifo Business Survey – Historical Business Expectations and Industrial Management Data
justification: A source of historical aggregated survey data on business expectations, industrial activity and economic conditions in Germany. Users can request time series covering 2000–2009, with breakdowns by industry, region and survey indicator where available. Particularly useful for studying business planning, management expectations, industrial confidence and strategic responses to changing economic conditions. Unlike confidential firm-level microdata, these aggregated historical series can be ordered directly from the ifo Institute.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2009
justification: A major longitudinal dataset covering individuals and households in Germany, including the entire 2000–2009 period. Particularly valuable for psychological research because it includes life satisfaction, subjective well-being, mental health, personality traits, and behavioral attitudes. The 2005 and 2009 surveys include Big Five personality measures covering openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism. Suitable for studying psychological changes over time and relationships between personality, employment, income, and well-being.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS), Baseline Study 2003–2006
justification: A nationally representative German health survey conducted between 2003 and 2006, covering children and adolescents aged 0–17. Includes psychological and mental health measures, emotional and behavioral difficulties, subjective health, and social determinants of mental well-being. The Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) provides indicators relevant to developmental and clinical psychology. Particularly useful for research on adolescent mental health, behavioral problems, and psychological development in Germany during the 2000s.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS1), 2008–2011
justification: A nationwide survey conducted by the Robert Koch Institute between November 2008 and November 2011. Covers adult mental health, psychological well-being, psychosocial risk factors, protective factors, and health-related behaviors. Particularly relevant to clinical psychology, health psychology, and psychiatric epidemiology. Although data collection extends into the 2010s, the study began during the requested decade and provides valuable evidence about psychological conditions in Germany at the end of the 2000s.

returned_title: German Family Panel (pairfam), 2008–2021
justification: A longitudinal German study beginning in 2008, with its first wave conducted in 2008–2009. Contains psychological and social information about romantic relationships, attachment, partnership satisfaction, parenting, child development, and intergenerational relationships. The initial sample included more than 12,000 individuals from three birth cohorts. Especially useful for developmental psychology, relationship psychology, family psychology, and research on psychological well-being within intimate relationships. Scientific-use data are available to researchers through GESIS.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: A cumulative dataset containing nationally representative German social surveys, including waves conducted in 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, and 2008. Provides information about social attitudes, values, trust, beliefs, interpersonal relationships, and social behavior. Useful for social psychology, political psychology, and research on attitudes and psychological correlates of social change in Germany. Its repeated cross-sectional design supports comparisons across the 2000s, although it is not primarily a clinical psychology dataset.

returned_title: German Health Update (GEDA), 2009
justification: A nationwide health survey conducted in Germany in 2009 by the Robert Koch Institute. The scientific-use dataset contains 21,262 observations and 316 variables. It is relevant to health psychology and mental health research because the GEDA survey program covers subjective health, psychological well-being, health-related stress, and behavioral risk factors. Particularly useful for investigating relationships between mental health, demographic characteristics, and health behaviors at the end of the 2000s. Access is provided through the Robert Koch Institute's research data infrastructure.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2008
justification: A historical release of Germany's longitudinal household panel covering the period through 2008. Particularly relevant to developmental and personality psychology because it includes adult psychological characteristics and information about children's socio-emotional development. The 2008 release introduced measures of personality and socio-emotional behavior among preschool-aged children, including a modified Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. Useful for examining family environments, child development, personality, and psychological well-being during the 2000s.

returned_title: German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS), Wave 1, 2009–2012
justification: A follow-up to the German KiGGS baseline survey, beginning in 2009. Contains information relevant to children's and adolescents' mental health, psychological development, behavioral difficulties, and health-related quality of life. Particularly valuable when combined with the 2003–2006 baseline study to examine changes in psychological outcomes over time. Although most data were collected after 2009, the study offers longitudinal research opportunities for individuals initially observed during the 2000s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Cumulation 1980–2008
justification: A cumulative historical dataset containing German population surveys conducted through 2008, including all five biennial survey waves from 2000 to 2008. Relevant to social psychology because it examines values, attitudes, social trust, political orientations, social relationships, and behavioral patterns. Especially useful for studying psychological aspects of social attitudes and their evolution during the 2000s. Unlike later cumulative releases, this historical version ends within the requested decade.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2006
justification: A historical release of the German Socio-Economic Panel containing observations through 2006. Particularly relevant for psychological research because SOEP introduced a revised health questionnaire module in 2002, repeated every two years, enabling analysis of health-related quality of life and psychological well-being. The dataset also includes personality-related measures, subjective life satisfaction, and social circumstances. Suitable for examining relationships between mental health, personality, employment, and living conditions in Germany during the first half of the 2000s.

returned_title: Eurostat – Digital Economy and Society Database
justification: One of the most comprehensive sources for studying digitalization in Germany during 2010–2019. Contains historical statistics on internet access, broadband connectivity, ICT adoption, e-commerce, digital skills, and digital technology use by households and businesses. Data can be filtered for Germany and individual years, allowing comparisons across the 2010s and with other European countries.

returned_title: Eurostat – Individuals: Internet Use
justification: Provides statistics on internet usage among individuals in European countries, including Germany. Includes observations from the 2010s and demographic breakdowns. Particularly useful for examining the spread of internet adoption, changes in usage frequency, and differences between population groups.

returned_title: Eurostat – Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals
justification: Provides information about access to research microdata from household and individual ICT surveys. Covers digital activities such as internet use, online shopping, digital skills, and cybersecurity. Historical survey modules include internet security in 2010, 2015, and 2019. Particularly valuable for investigating socioeconomic differences in digitalization within Germany. Microdata access is subject to eligibility requirements.

returned_title: European Commission – Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI)
justification: The European Commission's framework for measuring digital development across EU member states. Historical monitoring began in 2014, making it particularly useful for studying Germany's digital transformation during the second half of the 2010s. Indicators cover connectivity, human capital, internet services, business digitalization, and digital public services. Historical results enable comparisons between Germany and other EU countries.

returned_title: European Commission – Digital Decade DESI Visualization Tool
justification: Interactive platform for exploring European digitalization indicators, including historical data relevant to Germany during the 2010s. Covers broadband infrastructure, digital skills, business technology adoption, e-commerce, and digital public services. Provides dataset metadata and download services. Useful for visualizing trends and comparing Germany's digital performance with other EU countries, although historical coverage varies by indicator.

returned_title: World Bank – Individuals Using the Internet (% of Population), Germany
justification: Provides annual statistics on the percentage of Germany's population using the internet, including all years from 2010 through 2019. Based on International Telecommunication Union data. Particularly useful for analyzing long-term internet adoption, measuring changes in digital participation, and comparing Germany with other countries. Offers a straightforward historical indicator of digitalization.

returned_title: International Telecommunication Union – Internet Usage in Germany
justification: UNdata provides historical ICT statistics sourced from the International Telecommunication Union. The dataset includes annual internet usage percentages for Germany throughout 2010–2019. It is particularly suitable for tracking the diffusion of internet technology and comparing digital participation across years. The data can also support international comparisons using corresponding country records.

returned_title: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) – Internet Users for Germany
justification: Provides a historical time series measuring internet users per 100 people in Germany. The dataset includes annual observations covering the entire 2010–2019 period and originates from the World Bank's World Development Indicators. Useful for quantitative analysis, time-series modeling, and examining changes in digital adoption alongside economic indicators.

returned_title: Eurostat – Digital Economy and Society: Information on Data
justification: Official entry point explaining the structure and availability of Eurostat's digital economy datasets. Provides access to data covering household internet connections, individual internet use, e-commerce, e-government, business ICT adoption, and digital intensity. Particularly helpful for identifying indicators with observations from 2010–2019 and understanding their definitions, geographic coverage, and comparability.

returned_title: Our World in Data – Share of Individuals Using the Internet
justification: Provides a historical dataset and visualization of internet adoption in Germany, based on World Bank data. Includes observations covering the 2010s and supports comparisons with other countries. Particularly useful for quickly examining digitalization trends, producing visualizations, and downloading standardized time-series data.

returned_title: Eurostat – Employed Persons Working from Home by Professional Status (1992–2025)
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for studying telecommuting in Germany during the 2010s. Provides annual statistics on the percentage of employed people working from home, distinguishing between those who usually and sometimes work remotely. Data can be filtered for Germany and the years 2010–2019, with breakdowns by professional status and demographic characteristics. Particularly useful for analyzing historical trends in telecommuting before the COVID-19 pandemic.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Working Conditions and Home Office in Germany
justification: A representative survey of 20,012 employed individuals in Germany conducted in 2018 by the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB) and the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (BAuA). Particularly relevant because the survey includes information on access to home-office arrangements, actual home-office usage, working conditions, and occupational characteristics. Suitable for investigating which workers had access to telecommuting in Germany toward the end of the 2010s. Scientific-use microdata are available through a research data access procedure.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core) – Longitudinal Household Survey, 1984–2022
justification: A major longitudinal household panel survey conducted annually in Germany. Contains information about employment, working arrangements, household characteristics, income, and well-being. Questions about working from home appear in selected survey waves, including 2014, making the dataset useful for examining telecommuting patterns during the 2010s. Its longitudinal structure supports research on relationships between home-based work, employment outcomes, family circumstances, and individual characteristics. Researchers should consult the questionnaires to identify relevant variables and survey years.

returned_title: European Working Conditions Survey (EWCS) 2015 – Eurofound
justification: A European survey covering working conditions and employment arrangements, including approximately 2,000 respondents in Germany in 2015. Contains information relevant to workplace location, working time, work organization, and the use of information and communication technologies. Researchers can isolate German respondents to investigate working from home and related flexible employment arrangements. Particularly useful for comparing Germany with other European countries during the middle of the 2010s.
