returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics Database
justification: Official European statistical collection covering crime, policing, criminal proceedings, convictions, imprisonment and criminal justice personnel. Contains annual data covering the 2010s for EU countries and the United Kingdom. Particularly useful as a central entry point for constructing comparative country-year datasets on crime and criminal justice.

returned_title: Eurostat – Prison Capacity and Number of Persons Held (crim_pris_cap)
justification: Official Eurostat dataset measuring prison capacity and the number of incarcerated people across European countries. Relevant for studying incarceration, prison overcrowding, correctional systems and differences in criminal justice policies. Provides historical observations relevant to the 2010s, although data availability varies by country and year.

returned_title: Eurostat – Legal Cases Processed in First Instance Courts (crim_crt_case)
justification: European dataset covering criminal cases processed by first-instance courts, including legal status and court outcomes. Historical data extend from 2008, covering the requested 2010–2019 period. Useful for comparing criminal proceedings, court activity, convictions and acquittals across European judicial systems. Coverage and completeness vary by jurisdiction.

returned_title: Eurostat – Intentional Homicide and Sexual Offences by Legal Status and Sex (crim_hom_soff)
justification: Comparative crime and criminal justice dataset covering victims, suspected persons and convicted persons associated with intentional homicide and sexual offences. Includes sex-disaggregated information and historical observations from the 2010s. Relevant for investigating violent crime, sexual violence, gender differences and criminal justice outcomes across European countries.

returned_title: Eurostat – Police-Recorded Offences by NUTS 3 Region (crim_gen_reg)
justification: Regional crime dataset reporting police-recorded offences at the NUTS 3 geographical level. Includes crime categories such as intentional homicide and other serious offences. Contains observations from the 2010s for participating European countries. Especially useful for investigating geographical differences in crime within countries, although regional coverage is incomplete.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice Metadata
justification: Official metadata and dataset directory for European crime and criminal justice statistics. Documents police-recorded offences, criminal justice personnel, offenders, victims, court proceedings and prison populations. Covers data collected during the 2010s and explains national definitions, reporting practices and comparability limitations. Particularly valuable for identifying compatible variables across all requested countries.

returned_title: Council of Europe CEPEJ – Dynamic Database of European Judicial Systems
justification: Official comparative database maintained by the European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice. Contains country-level indicators on judicial budgets, judges, prosecutors, lawyers, court performance, case processing and judicial efficiency. Historical evaluation cycles include the 2010s. Covers European judicial systems, including those of the requested countries, subject to country-specific reporting availability. Particularly suitable for quantitative comparisons of judicial institutions.

returned_title: Council of Europe CEPEJ – Evaluation of European Judicial Systems, 2010–2012 Cycle
justification: Historical judicial systems evaluation covering the beginning of the requested decade. Includes comparative information about courts, judicial personnel, public prosecution, judicial expenditure, case processing and access to justice. Provides an important baseline for studying institutional changes in European legal systems throughout the 2010s.

returned_title: European Commission and CEPEJ – Studies on the Functioning of Judicial Systems in EU Member States (2018)
justification: European Commission publication containing CEPEJ studies and comparative statistical tables on the functioning of national judicial systems. Published in 2018 and covering EU Member States, including the United Kingdom before Brexit. Relevant indicators include court performance, judicial resources, case processing and institutional efficiency. Particularly useful for comparing legal systems during the latter half of the 2010s.

returned_title: Council of Europe CEPEJ – Judicial Systems Evaluation Tools and Historical Reports
justification: Official repository providing access to CEPEJ judicial evaluation resources, reports and comparative indicators. Historical evaluation cycles include observations from the 2010s. Relevant for studying judicial independence, court organization, legal professionals, judicial efficiency and national justice expenditures. Useful for building longitudinal datasets on European judicial systems.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Trust in the Legal System, Police and Political Institutions
justification: Comparative statistical dataset published by Statistics Netherlands using European Social Survey data. Includes country-level measurements of public trust in the legal system, police and other institutions. Historical survey waves cover the 2010s. Useful for studying perceived legitimacy of legal institutions and public confidence in law enforcement. Not every requested country participated in every survey wave.

returned_title: European Quality of Life Survey 2016 – Eurofound
justification: Large-scale European survey conducted in 2016, including all 28 countries requested. Contains information about trust in institutions, perceived social insecurity, public services and quality of society. Relevant for studying public confidence in police and legal institutions, perceptions of security and differences in institutional legitimacy across European countries.

returned_title: European Institute for Gender Equality – Trust in Institutions, European Quality of Life Survey
justification: Comparative dataset derived from Eurofound's European Quality of Life Survey, containing measurements of trust in public institutions, including the police. Provides observations for 2011 and 2016, as well as an earlier 2007 reference point. Useful for examining changes in public attitudes toward law enforcement and institutional legitimacy across EU countries during the 2010s.

returned_title: Eurostat — Police-Recorded Offences by Offence Category (crim_off_cat)
justification: One of the most relevant datasets for comparative crime analysis across the 28 requested European countries. Provides annual police-recorded crime statistics from 2008 onward, including the entire 2010–2019 period. Covers intentional homicide, assault, robbery, burglary, theft, sexual violence, and other offences classified using the International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes (ICCS). Data are available as absolute counts and rates per 100,000 inhabitants. The United Kingdom is represented through separate jurisdictions, including England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Particularly useful for examining cross-country differences and changes in recorded crime during the 2010s.

returned_title: Eurostat — Personnel in the Criminal Justice System by Sex (crim_just_job)
justification: Provides annual statistics on law enforcement and criminal justice personnel in European countries, including the requested countries during the 2010s. Includes police officers, professional judges, and prison personnel, with breakdowns by sex. Supports comparisons of police staffing levels, law enforcement capacity, gender representation, and criminal justice workforce trends. Particularly valuable for investigating whether changes in police personnel were associated with changes in crime rates between 2010 and 2019.

returned_title: Eurostat — Prison Capacity and Number of Persons Held (crim_pris_cap)
justification: Contains annual prison statistics covering 2008–2024, including the full 2010–2019 period. Provides measures of prison capacity and the number of people incarcerated across European jurisdictions. Suitable for studying imprisonment trends, prison overcrowding, detention rates, and differences in criminal justice systems. Covers the requested EU countries, with historical United Kingdom data reported by jurisdiction where available.

returned_title: Eurostat — Legal Cases Processed in First Instance Courts by Legal Status of the Court Process (crim_crt_case)
justification: Provides annual statistics on court proceedings from 2008 through 2022, encompassing the entire 2010s. Includes criminal cases brought before courts, resolved cases, and pending cases, alongside other categories of legal proceedings. Covers European Union countries and additional European jurisdictions. Useful for examining criminal court workloads, judicial efficiency, case backlogs, and differences in the administration of justice. Coverage varies by country and indicator, so missing observations should be checked before comparative analysis.

returned_title: Eurostat — Intentional Homicide and Sexual Offences by Legal Status and Sex of the Person Involved (crim_hom_soff)
justification: Provides detailed statistics on individuals involved in intentional homicide and sexual offences, including information on legal status and sex. Part of Eurostat's European crime and criminal justice statistical collection, which provides historical observations covering the 2010s. Particularly suitable for studying serious violent crime, sexual offences, suspected offenders, prosecutions, and convictions across the requested countries. Enables more detailed analysis than aggregate police-recorded crime statistics.

returned_title: Eurostat — Police-Recorded Offences by NUTS 3 Region (crim_gen_reg)
justification: Provides geographically disaggregated crime statistics for European regions using the NUTS classification. Relevant for examining regional differences in police-recorded crime within the requested countries, rather than relying exclusively on national averages. Can support research into urban-rural disparities, regional crime concentrations, and geographical patterns of criminal activity. Historical and geographical coverage varies across countries and offence categories; availability of individual years during 2010–2019 should be verified.

returned_title: Eurostat — Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics Database
justification: Official European statistical resource consolidating datasets on crime, law enforcement, criminal courts, prosecution, and prisons. Eurostat provides annual crime statistics beginning in 2008, including the full 2010–2019 period, with additional historical series. Covers the requested European Union countries and historical data for the United Kingdom, which was an EU member throughout the 2010s. Particularly useful as a starting point for identifying complementary datasets, downloading comparable country-year observations, and reviewing methodological differences between national statistical systems.

returned_title: Eurostat — Crime and Criminal Justice Reference Metadata
justification: Official metadata resource documenting the European crime and criminal justice statistical collection. Describes annual data covering police-recorded offences, criminal justice personnel, court proceedings, prosecutions, and prisons. Confirms that the statistical collection includes European countries from 2008 onward, covering the entire 2010s. Especially useful for identifying available statistical tables and assessing differences in offence definitions, reporting practices, counting methods, geographical coverage, and reference dates. This is a metadata and dataset-discovery resource rather than a standalone statistical table.

returned_title: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime — Intentional Homicide Victims
justification: Official UNODC dataset providing internationally harmonized statistics on intentional homicide victims. Relevant to the requested European countries and historical comparisons covering the 2010s, subject to country-year availability. Homicide is a particularly useful indicator for cross-national crime research because it is generally less affected by differences in reporting behavior than many other recorded offences. Suitable for analyzing homicide rates, victim characteristics, and long-term trends, and for comparing Eurostat crime indicators with an independent international statistical collection.

returned_title: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime — Crime and Criminal Justice Data Portal
justification: International statistical portal containing datasets on crime and criminal justice systems, including intentional homicide, recorded offences, criminal justice processes, and law enforcement indicators. UNODC collects official statistics from national authorities through the United Nations Survey of Crime Trends and Operations of Criminal Justice Systems. Relevant to all 28 requested countries and suitable for exploring historical crime and justice indicators during 2010–2019. Particularly valuable for cross-validating Eurostat statistics and identifying additional internationally comparable measures. Completeness varies by country, year, and indicator.

returned_title: European Institute for Gender Equality — Personnel in the Criminal Justice System
justification: European Institute for Gender Equality statistical dataset providing comparative information on criminal justice personnel, including police officers, with sex-disaggregated measures. The data interface supports examination of historical observations during the 2010s. Particularly useful for studying gender representation in law enforcement, differences in police personnel per 100,000 inhabitants, and changes in criminal justice workforce composition across European countries. Complements Eurostat's criminal justice personnel statistics and provides a relevant perspective on institutional characteristics.

returned_title: Eurobarometer Survey Data (2010–2019) – European Commission and GESIS
justification: One of the most comprehensive sources for studying international politics and organisations across all 28 countries specified. Includes surveys conducted throughout 2010–2019 covering public attitudes toward the European Union, European integration, EU institutions, international relations, foreign policy, migration, democracy, and political trust. Particularly suitable because all requested countries were EU members by 2013, including Croatia. Provides comparable country-level and individual-level survey data.

returned_title: Eurobarometer Primary Data and Documentation – GESIS
justification: Provides access to individual Eurobarometer datasets, questionnaires, codebooks, and survey documentation from the 2010s. Researchers can identify surveys addressing international organisations, European institutions, EU foreign policy, international cooperation, and political attitudes. Covers the requested EU member states, with Croatia included following its accession in 2013.

returned_title: Eurobarometer 74.2: Europe 2020, the Financial and Economic Crisis, and Information on European Political Matters (2010)
justification: A specific cross-national survey dataset from November–December 2010 examining European political affairs, the Europe 2020 strategy, and the financial and economic crisis. Relevant for analysing public perceptions of European governance, supranational institutions, and international political cooperation at the beginning of the decade. Covers EU member states participating in the survey.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS), Rounds 5–9 (2010–2018)
justification: Provides harmonised cross-national survey data collected approximately every two years, including rounds conducted in 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018. Contains measures of trust in the European Parliament, the United Nations, national political institutions, political participation, immigration attitudes, and European identity. Includes many of the requested countries, although participation varies by survey round. Particularly useful for comparing attitudes toward international organisations during the 2010s.

returned_title: Chapel Hill Expert Survey (CHES) – European Political Parties and EU Integration
justification: Provides expert assessments of European political parties' positions on European integration, EU policies, ideology, and related international political questions. Includes survey waves from 2010, 2014, and 2019, making it particularly relevant to the requested decade. Covers political parties across EU member states, including Central and Eastern European countries. Useful for analysing national political actors' relationships with supranational institutions and European integration.

returned_title: Chapel Hill Expert Survey Trend File, 1999–2019
justification: A harmonised longitudinal dataset combining Chapel Hill Expert Survey waves from 1999, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, and 2019. Includes political party positions on European integration, specific EU policies, and ideological orientations. Particularly valuable for comparing changes in political party attitudes toward European institutions across countries during the 2010s.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2014 – Voter Study, First Post-Election Survey
justification: Provides individual-level electoral and political attitude data collected following the 2014 European Parliament elections. Covers the 28 EU member states, matching the requested country list. Includes information about European political participation, electoral behaviour, political preferences, and attitudes toward European integration. Especially suitable for studying relationships between citizens, national political systems, and supranational democratic institutions.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2014 – Voter Study, Supplementary Study
justification: A supplementary dataset associated with the 2014 European Parliament elections. Contains measures relating to trust in EU institutions, European citizenship, identification with Europe, and perceptions of the European Parliament. Useful for investigating political legitimacy, supranational identity, and public attitudes toward European organisations during the middle of the 2010s.

returned_title: Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) – Historical Country-Year Datasets
justification: Provides longitudinal country-year datasets containing extensive indicators of democracy, political institutions, electoral systems, civil society, political accountability, and governance. Covers all 28 requested countries throughout 2010–2019. Particularly useful for comparing institutional and political developments across European countries and examining how national political systems relate to broader international democratic governance. Historical dataset versions can be accessed through the archive.

returned_title: European Observatory of Political Trust – Cross-National Political Trust Data
justification: Provides cross-national data on political trust and related institutional indicators for 44 European countries over the period 1980–2023, encompassing the entire 2010s. Integrates information from Eurobarometer, the European Social Survey, the European Values Study, the World Values Survey, and other sources. Relevant for investigating confidence in political institutions, democracy, government accountability, and institutional legitimacy across the requested European countries. Country and year availability should be checked for individual indicators.

returned_title: InDivEU – Political Party Preferences on Differentiated European Integration
justification: A research dataset addressing political party preferences concerning differentiated European integration. Incorporates information from the Chapel Hill Expert Survey waves of 2010, 2014, and 2019, alongside additional assessments of party positions. Particularly relevant for studying how political parties across European countries view participation in EU institutions, differentiated membership arrangements, and supranational governance. Useful for analysing international political cooperation and competing visions of European integration during the 2010s.

returned_title: Eurostat – General Government Expenditure by Function (COFOG)
justification: Provides comparable government expenditure statistics by function for European countries, including historical observations covering the 2010s. Relevant categories include general public services and foreign affairs-related expenditure, where separately available in the underlying classification. Useful for comparing the financial dimensions of international political engagement and public administration across the requested countries. The dataset is primarily financial rather than a direct measure of international organisations or diplomatic activity.

returned_title: Czech Social Science Data Archive (ČSDA) – Political Behaviour and Public Opinion Datasets, 2001–2009
justification: One of the most comprehensive sources of survey data on political behaviour and attitudes in the Czech Republic during the 2000s. The archive contains quantitative surveys dating from 2001 onward, including research on political participation, voting preferences, political trust, democratic values, and evaluations of government institutions. Particularly useful for identifying multiple datasets covering the decade.

returned_title: Public Opinion Research Centre (CVVM) – Our Society Survey Series, 2001–2009
justification: A collection of Czech public opinion surveys conducted regularly throughout the 2000s. Topics include political orientation, party identification, electoral preferences, satisfaction with democracy, confidence in political institutions, and attitudes toward the European Union. The repeated surveys are particularly valuable for examining changes in Czech political attitudes over time. Individual datasets and questionnaires are available through the archive.

returned_title: Our Society 2002 – February (Naše společnost 2002 – únor)
justification: An individual-level public opinion survey conducted by the Czech Public Opinion Research Centre in February 2002. It contains 1,083 observations and 176 variables, including questions concerning domestic politics and public attitudes. Particularly relevant for studying political opinions shortly before the 2002 Czech parliamentary election. The dataset includes survey data and questionnaire documentation.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – Czech Republic, Round 1 (2002–2003)
justification: A nationally representative cross-national survey containing Czech responses collected in 2002–2003. Relevant variables include political interest, voting participation, political trust, satisfaction with democracy, ideological orientation, and attitudes toward institutions. Particularly useful for establishing a baseline of Czech political attitudes at the beginning of the decade and comparing them with other European countries.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – Czech Republic, Round 4 (2008–2009)
justification: Provides individual-level survey data on Czech political attitudes and behaviour near the end of the 2000s. Includes measures of political participation, trust in parliament and politicians, satisfaction with government, political ideology, and social values. Particularly useful when combined with earlier ESS rounds to investigate changes in political attitudes during the decade, including the period surrounding the global financial crisis.

returned_title: Czech National Election Study (CNES) – 2002 and 2006 Parliamentary Elections
justification: The Czech National Election Study provides documentation for election surveys, including the 2006 parliamentary election. These studies are particularly relevant for research on voting behaviour, electoral participation, party choice, ideological identification, and political attitudes. The questionnaire repository helps identify relevant election-study variables, although access to the underlying microdata may require consulting the associated data archives.

returned_title: Party Preferences in the Czech Republic – 2000
justification: A dataset combining monthly Czech public opinion surveys conducted during 2000. It provides information on political party preferences and electoral attitudes throughout the year. Particularly useful for examining short-term fluctuations in party support and establishing a baseline for longitudinal studies of Czech political behaviour during the 2000s. The dataset is archived through GESIS.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Citizenship 2004
justification: The ISSP Citizenship 2004 study provides comparative survey measures concerning democratic citizenship, political participation, civic obligations, and attitudes toward government. Questions address what constitutes good citizenship, including obeying laws and monitoring government actions. The linked catalogue documents the international study; researchers should verify access to the Czech national sample through the ISSP or Czech Social Science Data Archive.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) – Role of Government 2006
justification: The 2006 ISSP Role of Government survey is relevant to Czech attitudes toward government responsibilities, public spending, state intervention, civil liberties, and the relationship between citizens and political institutions. It offers internationally comparable measures of political and economic attitudes during the middle of the decade. The Czech Social Science Data Archive identifies the 2006 module among the available ISSP research series.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Multilevel Data
justification: Provides contextual information that can be linked to individual European Social Survey responses, including observations from Czechia. Relevant contextual variables cover economic conditions, political institutions, demographics, and other country-level characteristics. Particularly useful for investigating whether changes in Czech political trust, voting behaviour, or satisfaction with democracy are associated with broader institutional and socioeconomic developments. Historical multilevel data are available for ESS Round 4 (2008–2009).

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Parliamentary Election Results (2002 and 2006)
justification: Official electoral datasets from the Czech Statistical Office (CZSO) covering elections to the Chamber of Deputies in 2002 and 2006. Includes political party results, votes, parliamentary seats, electoral participation, and geographical breakdowns. Particularly relevant for studying parliamentary representation, party competition, and the Czech political system during the 2000s.

returned_title: ParlGov – Parliaments and Governments Database
justification: Comparative political dataset containing information on Czech political parties, parliamentary elections, governing coalitions, and cabinet compositions throughout the 2000s. Provides information on government formation, party participation in cabinets, election outcomes, and political institutions. Particularly useful for examining government stability and coalition politics between 2000 and 2009.

returned_title: ParlGov – Czech Republic Cabinet History
justification: Country-specific dataset documenting successive Czech governments, including their formation dates, prime ministers, and governing parties. Covers government transitions throughout the 2000s, including the administrations of Miloš Zeman, Vladimír Špidla, Stanislav Gross, Jiří Paroubek, Mirek Topolánek, and Jan Fischer. Useful for analyzing changes in executive power, government composition, and coalition stability.

returned_title: Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) – Historical Democracy Indicators
justification: International longitudinal dataset measuring political institutions, democratic governance, electoral systems, civil liberties, judicial independence, and political accountability. Contains annual observations for the Czech Republic from 2000 to 2009. Suitable for investigating changes in democratic quality, political participation, institutional accountability, and government effectiveness.

returned_title: V-Dem – Varieties of Party Identity and Organization (V-Party)
justification: Dataset examining political party organization, ideological positioning, internal structures, and political behavior across countries, including the Czech Republic. Relevant historical observations can support research on Czech political parties during the 2000s, their ideological differences, organizational characteristics, and approaches to democratic governance.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Historical Election Results Database
justification: Official Czech statistical database providing detailed election results for political organizations and candidates. Includes historical election statistics with geographical breakdowns by municipality, district, and region. Particularly useful for examining voting patterns, political participation, and electoral support for Czech political parties during the 2000s.

returned_title: Czech Election Results by Municipality and Polling District (1996–2026)
justification: Harmonized dataset combining Czech parliamentary, Senate, European Parliament, regional, and municipal election results. Includes parliamentary elections in 2002 and 2006, regional elections in 2000, 2004, and 2008, and municipal elections in 2002 and 2006. Contains party-level results, candidate information, and geographical identifiers. Useful for studying political party competition and regional political differences throughout the 2000s.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Municipal Election Open Data (2002)
justification: Official machine-readable dataset covering the 2002 Czech municipal elections. Provides information on candidates, political parties, electoral lists, voting results, and local government representation. Particularly relevant for studying political organizations operating at the municipal level, local political competition, and decentralized governance in the early 2000s.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Municipal Election Open Data (2002 and 2006)
justification: Official collection of municipal election datasets, including elections held in 2002 and 2006. Supports longitudinal analysis of local government composition, party representation, candidate participation, and municipal political organizations. Particularly useful for comparing local electoral institutions and political developments across Czech municipalities.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Election Results for All Election Types Since 2004
justification: Official open-data resource covering multiple types of Czech elections from 2004 onward. Relevant to the 2004–2009 period, including parliamentary, regional, Senate, and European Parliament elections. Useful for comparing the electoral performance of political organizations across different levels of government.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Historical Parliamentary Elections (1920–2006)
justification: Historical electoral statistics compiled by the Czech Statistical Office covering parliamentary elections from 1920 through 2006. Includes results relevant to the 2002 and 2006 elections. Useful for placing political party developments and electoral changes during the 2000s in a longer historical context.

returned_title: Lijphart Elections Archive – Czech Republic
justification: Academic election archive containing historical district-level legislative election data for comparative political research. Includes Czech Republic electoral information within its historical coverage through 2003. Particularly relevant for studying the early 2000s, electoral geography, political party competition, and parliamentary election outcomes.

returned_title: Czech Political Candidate and Donation Datasets
justification: Research publication describing structured datasets of Czech political candidates and political donations. The candidate data integrate electoral results, party affiliations, constituency information, and candidate characteristics across election types. Relevant for studying political organizations, candidate networks, and electoral competition. Researchers should check the associated dataset documentation for the exact coverage of elections during 2000–2009.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Voter Turnout in Czech Elections Since 1996
justification: Structured historical dataset derived from official Czech election statistics, containing registered voters, participation rates, valid votes, and electoral turnout across election types. Includes observations from throughout the 2000s, including the 2002 and 2006 parliamentary elections and the 2004 and 2009 European Parliament elections. Useful for examining political participation and public engagement with democratic institutions.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Statistical Yearbook of the Czech Republic 2003
justification: Official statistical yearbook containing tables on Czech political institutions and electoral outcomes. Includes results of the 2002 local elections, votes and seats obtained by political parties and movements, and results of the June 2003 referendum on Czech accession to the European Union. Particularly valuable for researching local government, political representation, and European integration during the early 2000s.

returned_title: Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) – Czech Republic Parliamentary Election Data, 2006
justification: Historical parliamentary election data from the Inter-Parliamentary Union covering the Czech Republic's 2006 Chamber of Deputies election. Provides information on the electoral process, parliamentary composition, political party representation, and election outcomes. Useful for analyzing the Czech parliamentary system and political party competition in 2006.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Election Results for All Election Types Since 2004
justification: Official dataset collection published by the Czech Statistical Office (CZSO). Contains historical results for parliamentary, Senate, regional, municipal, and European Parliament elections. Provides election results at multiple geographic levels, including municipalities and polling districts. Data are available in XML and Excel formats. Particularly useful for comprehensive analysis of Czech elections between 2004 and 2009.

returned_title: Czech Parliamentary Election Results – 2002
justification: Official open dataset covering the 2002 elections to the Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Parliament. Contains voting results, political party performance, and electoral statistics. Useful for investigating party competition, geographic voting patterns, and electoral participation during the early 2000s.

returned_title: Czech Parliamentary Election Results – 2006
justification: Official Czech Statistical Office dataset documenting the 2006 parliamentary elections. Includes election results, political party votes, and geographic breakdowns. Particularly valuable for comparing the 2002 and 2006 parliamentary elections and studying changes in political preferences.

returned_title: Czech Senate Election Results – 1996–2025
justification: Comprehensive official dataset covering elections to the Czech Senate, including elections held in 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, and 2008. Contains candidate information, electoral districts, voting results, and polling-district-level data. Includes downloadable data in XML, Excel, CSV, and JSON formats. Suitable for longitudinal research on Czech Senate elections throughout the 2000s.

returned_title: Czech Senate Elections – Complete Historical Data and Candidate Registers
justification: Official downloadable data collection containing candidate registers, political party classifications, electoral district identifiers, and historical Senate election data from 1996 through 2025. Includes all regular Senate elections held during the 2000s. Particularly useful for candidate-level analysis, party affiliation research, and comparisons across election years.

returned_title: Czech Senate Election Results – 2008
justification: Official dataset specifically documenting the 2008 Czech Senate elections. Provides election results and supporting electoral data in open formats. Useful for studying candidate performance, voting patterns, and electoral competition in the final years of the 2000s.

returned_title: Czech Regional Elections – 2000
justification: Official Czech Statistical Office open dataset containing results from the 2000 regional council elections. Provides information on regional electoral competition and voting outcomes. Particularly useful for examining the development of regional politics and electoral behavior at the beginning of the decade.

returned_title: Czech Regional Elections – 2004
justification: Official dataset covering the 2004 elections to regional councils in the Czech Republic. Contains regional election results and supporting electoral statistics. Enables comparisons with the 2000 regional elections and analysis of changing political preferences across Czech regions.

returned_title: Czech Municipal Elections – 2002
justification: Official open dataset documenting the 2002 municipal council elections. Contains local election results and related electoral information. Particularly relevant for studying local political competition, independent candidates, and voting behavior across Czech municipalities.

returned_title: Czech European Parliament Elections – 2009
justification: Official Czech Statistical Office documentation describing the XML election-results data for the 2009 European Parliament elections. Provides information about the structure and availability of electoral results. Useful for researchers examining European electoral participation and political party performance in the Czech Republic during the late 2000s.

returned_title: Czech European Parliament Elections – Polling District Data, 2004–2014
justification: Official data documentation for polling-district-level European Parliament election results covering 2004 through 2014, including both the 2004 and 2009 elections. Describes variables such as registered voters, ballots issued, valid votes, political party votes, and candidate preference votes. Useful for researchers working with granular European election data.

returned_title: Czech Election Results by Municipality and Polling District – 1996–2026
justification: Harmonized historical election dataset combining Czech Statistical Office election results into a consistent structure. Covers parliamentary elections in 2002 and 2006; European Parliament elections in 2004 and 2009; regional elections in 2000, 2004, and 2008; municipal elections in 2002 and 2006; and Senate elections throughout the decade. Provides standardized geographic identifiers and multiple data formats, including CSV, JSON, Parquet, and PostgreSQL. Particularly valuable for longitudinal analysis and geographic comparisons. This is a third-party processed dataset rather than an official CZSO release.

returned_title: Voter Turnout in Czech Elections Since 1996
justification: Historical election participation dataset derived from Czech Statistical Office records. Includes elections held throughout the 2000–2009 period, with information on registered voters, ballots issued, valid votes, and voter turnout percentages. Covers multiple election types and is particularly useful for comparing electoral participation across years and election categories.

returned_title: Czech Statistical Office – Election Results in the Public Database
justification: Official Czech Statistical Office resource describing election results available through its public statistical database. Includes information about the 2006 parliamentary elections and geographic breakdowns covering municipalities, districts, regions, and other administrative areas. Useful for researchers interested in integrating election results with demographic and regional statistical indicators.

returned_title: Statistical Yearbook of the Czech Republic 2003 – Election Statistics
justification: Official statistical publication containing historical election tables, including results from the 2002 municipal and Senate elections. Includes information about votes, seats, political parties, and independent candidates. Provides useful supplementary historical statistics for analyzing elections in the early 2000s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) 2013: National Identity III – Netherlands
justification: Highly relevant dataset specifically examining cultural and national identity in the Netherlands. Data were collected between April and September 2014 from 1,638 respondents. The survey includes 130 variables covering national pride, national identity, attitudes toward immigration, minorities, cultural belonging, and international relations. Particularly suitable for analyzing how Dutch people understood national identity during the 2010s.

returned_title: LISS Panel: Nationalism and the National Dimension of Cultural Consumption – Wave 1 (2011)
justification: A nationally representative panel survey conducted in September 2011 examining relationships between Dutch national identity, nationalism, social class, and cultural consumption. The dataset includes questions about Dutch identity, national pride, attachment to other Dutch citizens, and preferences for Dutch films, books, and music. Approximately 4,785 respondents participated. Particularly useful for studying connections between cultural practices and national belonging.

returned_title: LISS Panel: Nationalism and the National Dimension of Cultural Consumption – Wave 2 (2013)
justification: Follow-up survey conducted in September 2013 with approximately 3,805 respondents from the original study. Includes measures of national identification, cultural preferences, perceptions of foreign cultural influences, and emotional attachment to the Netherlands. Questions address whether Dutch identity is personally important and whether exposure to foreign cultural products threatens national culture. Especially valuable for examining changes in national identity between 2011 and 2013.

returned_title: Social and Cultural Report 2018: Dutch Identity – Part 2
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for studying Dutch national identity during the late 2010s. Collected between July and September 2018 by CentERdata for the Netherlands Institute for Social Research (SCP). Investigates what respondents consider characteristic of the Netherlands and which factors contribute to their feelings of national connectedness. Particularly appropriate for studying cultural symbols, collective identity, national belonging, and perceptions of Dutch society.

returned_title: LISS Immigrant Panel: Multiculturalism (2010)
justification: Survey conducted in August 2010 investigating multiculturalism and immigrant acculturation in the Netherlands. Includes attitudes toward cultural diversity, preservation of minority cultures, social integration, and national unity. Particularly useful for analyzing how immigrants negotiate cultural identity and how multiculturalism relates to Dutch national identity during the early 2010s.

returned_title: ISSP Netherlands 2013–2014: Citizenship and National Identity
justification: Dutch dataset combining the International Social Survey Programme's National Identity III and Citizenship II modules. Data were collected in 2014 by researchers at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Covers national identity, citizenship, political participation, social belonging, and attitudes toward national communities. The complete Dutch dataset contains more information than the Netherlands subset of the international ISSP release, making it useful for detailed country-specific research.

returned_title: Cultural Changes in the Netherlands (Culturele Veranderingen in Nederland) – 2010s Survey Series
justification: Long-running survey program conducted by the Netherlands Institute for Social Research (SCP), examining Dutch attitudes toward society and culture. Includes survey waves throughout the 2010s and provides opportunities to investigate changing social values, cultural attitudes, and perceptions of Dutch society. Especially useful for longitudinal analysis of cultural identity and social change. The linked official page explains the survey and directs researchers to archived datasets.

returned_title: Cultural Changes in the Netherlands and SCP Living Conditions Index (CVSLI 2018)
justification: Official SCP dataset from 2018 combining information on cultural and social attitudes with indicators of living conditions in the Netherlands. Relevant for investigating cultural values, social differences, and attitudes toward Dutch society in the late 2010s. Can support analysis of how demographic and socioeconomic characteristics relate to cultural identity and perceptions of national community.

returned_title: Survey Integration of Minorities (SIM 2015) – Netherlands
justification: Survey dataset from the Netherlands Institute for Social Research focusing on the integration of minority populations in Dutch society. Relevant for studying ethnic and cultural identity, immigrant integration, minority experiences, and relationships between cultural background and belonging in the Netherlands. Particularly useful for examining national identity from the perspective of ethnic minorities during the middle of the 2010s.

returned_title: LISS Panel: Nostalgia 2019 – Wave 2
justification: Survey conducted in 2019 examining collective nostalgia, national identity, and group dynamics in the Netherlands. Includes questions about Dutch cultural change, feelings toward the country's past, and attitudes about national identity. Particularly valuable for analyzing relationships between cultural nostalgia, national belonging, and perceptions of changing Dutch traditions at the end of the 2010s.

returned_title: Survey on the Integration of Minorities (SIM) 2011 – Netherlands
justification: Conducted by the Netherlands Institute for Social Research (SCP), this dataset examines the integration of ethnic minority populations in the Netherlands in 2010–2011. It focuses on people of Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, and Dutch Antillean origin. It is particularly relevant for studying social integration, discrimination, education, employment, cultural identity, and relations between ethnic groups during the early 2010s.

returned_title: Survey on the Integration of Minorities (SIM) 2015 – Version 3
justification: A comprehensive survey conducted in 2015 examining ethnic minority integration in Dutch society. It includes Turkish, Moroccan, Surinamese, Dutch Caribbean, Polish, and Somali populations, alongside respondents without a migration background. The dataset contains information about social participation, discrimination, cultural integration, and socioeconomic conditions. It is particularly useful for comparing minority experiences across ethnic groups and examining changes between 2011 and 2015. Access may be restricted.

returned_title: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) – Population by Migration Background, Sex and Age, 1972–2022
justification: An official statistical dataset containing historical demographic information about Netherlands residents with migration backgrounds. It covers the entire 2010–2019 period and enables analysis of population size, demographic composition, age, sex, and migration backgrounds. Particularly useful for examining changes in the relative sizes of minority populations throughout the decade and comparing demographic trends across different origin groups.

returned_title: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) – Population Development by Migration Background and Generation, 1996–2021
justification: An official longitudinal dataset covering demographic changes among population groups with different migration backgrounds. It includes the entire 2010s and distinguishes migration backgrounds and generations. Researchers can use it to study migration patterns, population growth, and demographic changes affecting minority communities, including differences between first-generation and second-generation migrant populations.

returned_title: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) – Households by Migration Background, 2001–2019
justification: Provides historical statistics on Dutch households categorized by migration background. Its coverage includes the 2010–2019 period, making it suitable for studying household characteristics and demographic differences among ethnic and migrant-origin populations. Particularly useful for research into family structures, household composition, and the changing demographic characteristics of minority communities.

returned_title: LISS Panel – Longitudinal Internet Studies for the Social Sciences
justification: A longitudinal survey infrastructure containing extensive information about individuals and households in the Netherlands. Its annual core studies and demographic background variables provide opportunities to examine ethnicity, migration background, employment, education, political attitudes, religion, and social integration throughout the 2010s. The longitudinal structure makes it particularly valuable for investigating changes in minority experiences over time. Data are available for scientific and policy-relevant research subject to a user agreement.

returned_title: LISS Immigrant Panel – Netherlands, 2010–2014
justification: A specialized immigrant panel operated alongside the regular LISS panel between October 2010 and December 2014. It provides opportunities to study immigrant populations and their socioeconomic circumstances, attitudes, and experiences in Dutch society. Particularly relevant for research focusing specifically on migrant-origin minorities during the early 2010s. The panel's longitudinal design is useful for examining changes in individual experiences and integration outcomes.

returned_title: Netherlands Institute for Social Research (SCP) – Survey Integration of Migrants (SIM) Data Collection
justification: The official research documentation and dataset information page for the Dutch Survey on the Integration of Migrants. It provides methodological details about the 2011 and 2015 survey waves, including target populations, sampling methods, response rates, and data collection procedures. Particularly valuable for identifying comparable minority integration datasets and understanding methodological differences between survey waves.

returned_title: SCP Open Data – Netherlands Institute for Social Research
justification: The official open-data catalogue of the Netherlands Institute for Social Research. It provides dataset references and DOIs for studies relevant to ethnic minorities, migration, integration, and social inequality. Particularly useful for locating the SIM 2011 and SIM 2015 datasets and other Dutch social surveys conducted during the 2010s. The catalogue also includes broader social research datasets that may support comparative analysis.

returned_title: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) – Open Data StatLine
justification: The official Dutch statistical data portal provides access to demographic, socioeconomic, education, employment, and migration datasets. Historical tables allow researchers to investigate minority populations during 2010–2019, including differences by migration background and geographic location. It is especially useful for obtaining standardized quantitative indicators and constructing longitudinal comparisons across the decade.

returned_title: Differences in the Netherlands 2019 (Verschil in Nederland 2019 – ViN2019)
justification: A 2019 social research dataset produced by the Netherlands Institute for Social Research. It is relevant to investigating social differences and inequality within Dutch society. It can complement minority-focused datasets when examining socioeconomic disparities and social divisions toward the end of the 2010s. Researchers should inspect its documentation to establish which migration-background variables and minority-group comparisons are available.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2014 – Euromanifesto Study
justification: Highly relevant dataset covering political party manifestos for the 2014 European Parliament elections, including the Netherlands. Contains coded information about political parties' positions on European integration, EU institutions, international cooperation, and European policy issues. Particularly useful for analyzing Dutch political parties' approaches to international organizations and European governance during the 2010s.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2014 – Voter Study, First Post-Election Survey
justification: Cross-national survey dataset covering the 2014 European Parliament elections, including Dutch respondents. Provides information about political attitudes, electoral behavior, perceptions of EU institutions, and preferences concerning European integration. Suitable for investigating Dutch public opinion toward international and European political organizations.

returned_title: Political Parties' Policy Positions for the 2014 Elections to the European Parliament
justification: Dataset containing the policy positions of 231 political parties across 28 European countries, including the Netherlands, on 30 issues relevant to the 2014 European Parliament elections. Useful for comparing Dutch parties' positions on European integration and international political issues with those of parties in other EU member states.

returned_title: United Nations General Assembly Resolutions: Voting Data and Issue Categories
justification: International politics dataset covering United Nations General Assembly resolutions and voting behavior from 1995 to 2022, including the entire 2010–2019 period. Dutch voting records can be extracted to analyze the Netherlands' positions on international security, human rights, development, and other global governance issues. Particularly useful for studying Dutch foreign policy within the United Nations.

returned_title: United Nations General Assembly Voting, 1946–2013
justification: Dataset created by Andreas Warntjen and published through Harvard Dataverse, documenting voting behavior in the United Nations General Assembly from 1946 to 2013. Includes the Netherlands and covers the early 2010s. Records votes in categories such as yes, no, abstention, and absence. Useful for researching Dutch diplomatic alignment, international cooperation, and participation in multilateral decision-making.

returned_title: Correlates of War – Intergovernmental Organizations Dataset, Version 3.0
justification: Comprehensive dataset tracking membership in intergovernmental organizations worldwide from 1815 to 2014. Includes annual country-level membership information for the Netherlands during 2010–2014. Particularly relevant for studying Dutch participation in international organizations, changes in institutional memberships, and the Netherlands' position within global governance networks.

returned_title: OECD Development Finance Statistics – Data on Flows to Developing Countries
justification: Official OECD dataset providing detailed information about international development assistance and financial flows. Includes the Netherlands as a donor country and supports analysis of Dutch development cooperation during 2010–2019. Relevant variables include official development assistance, recipient countries, funding channels, and contributions through multilateral organizations. Useful for examining the Netherlands' international development policies and relationships with global institutions.

returned_title: Dutch Parliamentary Election Study 2010
justification: National survey dataset examining Dutch voters' political attitudes before and after the 2010 parliamentary election. Contains questions about European unification, EU membership, international military missions, and political institutions. Particularly relevant for investigating how international political issues influenced Dutch electoral preferences and public opinion at the beginning of the 2010s.

returned_title: Standard Eurobarometer 74
justification: European Commission public opinion survey conducted in 2010, covering the Netherlands alongside other European countries. Provides a basis for studying Dutch citizens' attitudes toward European institutions, EU policies, and European integration. Particularly useful for cross-national comparisons of political trust and public perceptions of international and supranational governance.

returned_title: European Election Studies – 2014 and 2019
justification: Collection of European election research datasets maintained through GESIS, including studies conducted during the 2014 and 2019 European Parliament elections. The Netherlands is included in the comparative research framework. Relevant data cover European political identity, voter behavior, political representation, attitudes toward EU institutions, and European integration. Useful for comparing changes in Dutch attitudes toward European governance throughout the decade.

returned_title: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database
justification: Internationally recognized dataset containing annual military expenditure statistics for the Netherlands throughout 2010–2019. Includes spending measured in national currency, US dollars, and as a percentage of GDP. Relevant to international politics because it supports analysis of Dutch defense policy, NATO burden-sharing, military commitments, and international security cooperation during the 2010s.

returned_title: SIPRI – Netherlands National Reports on Arms Exports
justification: Collection of Dutch national reports documenting arms export policies and licensing decisions, with reports available for individual years throughout 2010–2019. Provides primary-source information about the Netherlands' international arms trade, export controls, and military cooperation. Useful for investigating the relationship between Dutch foreign policy, international security organizations, and global arms regulation.

returned_title: European Parliament Election Study 2014 – Euromanifesto Study Documentation and Data
justification: GESIS dataset access and documentation page for the 2014 Euromanifesto Study. Provides research data on party programs for the European Parliament elections, including Dutch political parties. Particularly useful for detailed content analysis of positions on EU institutions, international cooperation, European political integration, and supranational governance during the 2014 election.

returned_title: CBS – Immigration and Emigration by Sex, Age, Country of Birth and Region (2010–2021)
justification: Official dataset from Statistics Netherlands (CBS) covering immigration and emigration between 2010 and 2021. Includes breakdowns by sex, age, country of birth and geographical region. Particularly relevant because it covers the entire 2010–2019 period and allows detailed analysis of migration patterns across demographic groups.

returned_title: CBS – External Migration by Sex, Age, Marital Status and Country of Birth (1995–2022)
justification: Comprehensive historical dataset published by Statistics Netherlands. Contains annual immigration, emigration and net migration figures, including administrative corrections. Provides demographic breakdowns by sex, age, marital status and country of birth. Suitable for examining migration trends during the 2010s and comparing them with earlier periods.

returned_title: CBS – Population and Population Dynamics by Month (1995–2018)
justification: Official monthly demographic dataset covering most of the 2010s. Includes immigration, emigration, population growth and internal migration indicators. Particularly useful for studying monthly migration fluctuations, seasonal patterns and relationships between migration and population change in the Netherlands.

returned_title: Eurostat – Immigration by Age Group, Sex and Citizenship
justification: European statistical dataset containing annual immigration figures categorized by citizenship, sex and age. Data can be filtered for the Netherlands and the years 2010–2019. Useful for studying the nationality composition of immigrants and comparing Dutch immigration patterns with those of other European countries.

returned_title: Eurostat – Immigration Statistics: Annual Immigration
justification: Eurostat dataset providing annual immigration totals for European countries, including the Netherlands. Supports analysis of changes in immigration volumes throughout the 2010s and comparisons with other EU member states. Particularly appropriate for descriptive statistics and international comparisons.

returned_title: Eurostat – International Migration and Citizenship Statistics
justification: Official Eurostat data portal providing access to datasets on immigration, emigration, citizenship and migration-related demographic characteristics. Includes historical annual statistics relevant to the Netherlands during 2010–2019. Useful for identifying multiple complementary datasets and conducting comparative European migration research.

returned_title: CBS – Immigration, Emigration and Net Migration in the Netherlands
justification: Official Statistics Netherlands data publication containing annual immigration, emigration and net migration figures, including every year from 2010 through 2019. Provides a straightforward historical time series suitable for examining the growth of immigration and changes in net migration during the decade.

returned_title: CBS – Emigration Statistics and Population Dynamics
justification: Official CBS statistical dashboard providing emigration figures and access to downloadable data. Useful for examining departures from the Netherlands, studying emigration trends and complementing immigration statistics. The underlying population dynamics statistics support historical migration analysis.

returned_title: Dutch Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) – Migration Radar
justification: Official Dutch government source containing historical publications and statistics on asylum migration. Includes reports from 2019 with information on asylum applications and migration developments. Particularly relevant for studying refugee and asylum-related migration toward the end of the 2010s, although it does not provide a complete decade-long dataset.

returned_title: Eurostat – Managed Migration Statistics
justification: Official European statistical portal providing datasets on residence permits, immigration enforcement and other managed migration indicators. Includes annual and quarterly statistical series that can be used to investigate migration administration in the Netherlands during the 2010s. Useful for research focused on non-EU migration, residence authorizations and immigration policy.

returned_title: CBS – Historical Migration Timeline in the Netherlands (1849–2025)
justification: Historical statistical publication from Statistics Netherlands containing annual immigration, emigration and net migration figures for 2010–2019, alongside a much longer historical series. Includes contextual information about migration from European countries and changes associated with EU enlargement. Useful for historical comparisons and understanding structural developments in Dutch migration.

returned_title: Election and Social Data of the Districts and Municipalities of the German Reich, 1920–1933 (GESIS ZA8013)
justification: Highly relevant historical dataset covering the German Reich during the 1920s and early 1930s. Contains Reichstag election results from 1920 to 1933, population statistics, religious composition, occupational structure, and unemployment figures at district and municipal levels. Particularly valuable for studying political change, socioeconomic conditions, and the rise of National Socialism.

returned_title: German Weimar Republic Data, 1919–1933 (ICPSR 42)
justification: Comprehensive historical dataset covering electoral and demographic developments in Germany during the Weimar Republic. Includes Reichstag elections from 1920 to 1933, presidential elections in 1925 and 1932, national referendums, and demographic information from the 1925 German census. Useful for investigating voting behavior, political radicalization, and demographic changes.

returned_title: Voters and Elections in the Weimar Republic, 1920–1933
justification: Historical electoral dataset focusing on political participation and voting patterns during the Weimar Republic. Includes information about electoral constituencies, social structures, and selected election results between 1924 and 1933. Relevant for studying the development of German parliamentary democracy and the political transformations preceding Nazi rule.

returned_title: Historical Statistics of Germany (HISTAT)
justification: Historical statistical database containing time-series data on Germany's economic, demographic, and social development. Its historical coverage includes the 1920s and 1930s, making it useful for studying inflation, unemployment, industrial development, population changes, and the economic consequences of the Great Depression. Provides access to downloadable historical statistical series.

returned_title: Historical Statistical Yearbooks of the German Reich (University of Mannheim Research Data Center)
justification: Research data resource providing access to historical statistical yearbooks covering Germany from 1880 onward. Includes economic, demographic, social, and health statistics relevant to the German Reich during the 1920s and 1930s. Particularly useful for examining industrial production, employment, population development, public finances, and living conditions during the Weimar Republic and early Nazi period.

returned_title: Historical German Economic Development, 1820–1929 (GESIS ZA8084)
justification: Historical economic time-series dataset documenting Germany's economic development through 1929. Includes the 1920s and provides a longer historical perspective for analyzing economic conditions during the Weimar Republic. Useful for examining economic recovery, structural changes, and developments preceding the Great Depression.

returned_title: Money Supply, Prices, National Income and National Debt in Germany, Including the National Socialist Period (GESIS ZA8231)
justification: Historical economic statistics resource containing time-series data on monetary developments, prices, national income, and public debt. Includes coverage of the National Socialist period from 1933 to 1945. Relevant for researching economic policy, government financing, monetary conditions, and economic transformations in Germany during the 1930s.

returned_title: Historical Development of the German Financial System (GESIS ZA8230)
justification: Historical statistical dataset documenting the development of Germany's financial system over time. Provides economic and financial time series useful for analyzing the interwar German economy, banking and financial structures, and monetary developments. Relevant to research on financial instability and economic conditions during the Weimar Republic and the 1930s.

returned_title: German Reich Election and Social Statistics, 1920–1933 (GESIS Knowledge Graph ZA8013)
justification: Structured metadata record for the historical election and social statistics dataset compiled by Jürgen W. Falter and Dirk Hänisch. Identifies original sources including election statistics, unemployment statistics, population censuses, housing censuses, and occupational censuses. Particularly useful for identifying historical variables and tracing statistical sources concerning the German Reich between 1920 and 1933.

returned_title: Reichstag Elections in the Weimar Republic, 1919–1933 (German History in Documents and Images)
justification: Historical electoral data visualization covering German parliamentary elections between 1919 and 1933. Presents constituency-level election results through interactive maps, allowing researchers to examine regional voting patterns, party support, and changes in the political geography of the German Reich. Especially relevant for studying the electoral rise of the Nazi Party and the decline of Weimar democracy. This is a visual historical data resource rather than a conventional downloadable dataset.

returned_title: Correlates of War: Intergovernmental Organizations (IGO) Dataset, 1815–2014
justification: Highly relevant for studying Germany's participation in international organizations during the 1980s. Contains historical data on membership in intergovernmental organizations, including country-year and organization-year records. Researchers can examine West Germany (Federal Republic of Germany) and East Germany (German Democratic Republic) separately, investigating their international institutional relationships during the Cold War. Annual observations cover the entire 1980–1989 period.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Database: Political Party Programs and International Policy Positions
justification: Provides quantitative information derived from political party election manifestos, including those associated with West German federal elections in 1980, 1983, and 1987. Particularly useful for analyzing political parties' positions on international relations, European integration, military policy, peace, and foreign affairs. Enables comparisons of international policy priorities across major West German political organizations, including the CDU/CSU, SPD, FDP, and Greens.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), 1980–2023
justification: A major longitudinal survey program documenting political attitudes, social values, and institutional trust among the German population. Beginning in 1980, the survey provides observations throughout the 1980s, particularly for West Germany. Useful for examining political orientations, party preferences, attitudes toward institutions, and public opinion in the context of Cold War politics. Researchers should check individual survey questionnaires to identify variables specifically related to international politics and organizations.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS): Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: Combines multiple waves of German social survey data into a longitudinally comparable dataset. Includes observations from the 1980s and facilitates analysis of changing political attitudes during the final decade of German division. Particularly suitable for investigating political ideology, institutional confidence, political participation, and public attitudes toward government. The cumulative structure makes it easier to compare political developments across multiple years.

returned_title: Eurobarometer: European Community, April 1981 (ICPSR 7959)
justification: A historical public opinion survey examining attitudes toward European Community institutions and international political relationships. Includes respondents from West Germany and other European Community countries. Particularly relevant for investigating German perceptions of European integration, relations between nations, NATO, the United States, and the Eastern European bloc during the early 1980s. Provides an international comparative perspective on West German political attitudes.

returned_title: Manifesto Project Database: Historical German Election Manifestos
justification: Offers access to historical election programs and standardized political position measurements. For the 1980s, researchers can investigate how West German political parties addressed NATO membership, East–West relations, European cooperation, disarmament, and international security. Especially valuable for studying the institutional and ideological positions of political organizations during the Cold War and comparing changes between the 1980, 1983, and 1987 federal elections.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS): Political Attitudes and Institutional Trust
justification: The GESIS research data catalogue provides access to individual ALLBUS survey waves, including surveys conducted in 1980, 1982, 1984, 1986, and 1988. These datasets allow researchers to select specific historical periods and investigate political participation, political party identification, institutional confidence, and broader political orientations. Individual questionnaires should be consulted to determine whether questions about international relations or organizations were included in each wave.

returned_title: Correlates of War: International Organization Membership by Country and Year
justification: The country-year component of the Correlates of War IGO collection is particularly useful for quantitative historical research on international organizations. By filtering observations to East and West Germany between 1980 and 1989, researchers can reconstruct and compare their memberships in international governmental organizations. The data can support research on diplomatic integration, international institutional participation, Cold War bloc structures, and differences between the two German states.

returned_title: European Protest and Coercion Data (1980–1995) – Ron Francisco
justification: One of the most directly relevant datasets for studying conflict, security, and peace in Germany during the 1980s. Contains event-level information on political protests, demonstrations, strikes, riots, and state coercion across European countries. Includes separate records for West Germany (Federal Republic of Germany) and East Germany (German Democratic Republic). Particularly valuable for investigating the peace movement, political opposition, state repression, and civil unrest during the Cold War.

returned_title: European Protest and Coercion Data – German Democratic Republic (1980–1990)
justification: A dataset review and access guide specifically focused on political protest and coercion in East Germany. The underlying dataset contains more than 1,100 event records covering January 1, 1980, through October 3, 1990. Documents protests, strikes, rallies, riots, and government repression. Especially relevant for studying East German peace activism, opposition movements, political resistance, and the events leading to the peaceful revolution of 1989. The linked review provides information about accessing the original dataset and codebook.

returned_title: PRODAT – Documentation and Analysis of Protest Events in the Federal Republic of Germany (1950–2002)
justification: Historical protest-event dataset developed by the WZB Berlin Social Science Center. Covers West German protests throughout the 1980s, including demonstrations associated with peace movements, nuclear disarmament, political mobilization, and social conflicts. Based on systematic analysis of newspaper reporting. Particularly useful for examining the scale, frequency, and development of anti-nuclear and peace demonstrations during the NATO missile deployment controversy. The project page provides access to historical protest data.

returned_title: Global Terrorism Database (GTD) – Germany, 1980–1989
justification: International event-level dataset documenting terrorist incidents beginning in 1970. Researchers can filter records by Germany and the years 1980–1989 to examine political violence, bombings, assassinations, attacks on military installations, and other terrorist activities. Particularly useful for investigating left-wing terrorism, including the Red Army Faction, and security threats affecting West Germany during the Cold War. Contains information on incident dates, locations, attack methods, targets, perpetrators, and casualties.

returned_title: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database – Germany (1980–1989)
justification: Military expenditure dataset maintained by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, with historical coverage beginning in 1949. Provides annual military spending indicators relevant to West Germany throughout the 1980s. Variables include military expenditure in national currency, US dollars, and as a percentage of GDP. Particularly useful for examining defense spending, militarization, NATO commitments, and the financial dimensions of Cold War security policies. Historical German observations should be interpreted with attention to the division between East and West Germany.

returned_title: World Bank World Development Indicators – Military Expenditure (% of GDP), Germany
justification: Country-level time-series data on military expenditure as a percentage of GDP, sourced from SIPRI. The linked page is configured to display historical German observations through 1989. Suitable for quantitative research examining defense spending, military priorities, and Cold War security policies in West Germany. Particularly useful for comparing military expenditure with economic indicators and examining changes associated with NATO defense strategies during the 1980s.

returned_title: Correlates of War – National Material Capabilities Dataset
justification: Longitudinal international dataset containing annual measures of national military and material capabilities from 1816 through 2022. Includes military expenditure, military personnel, population, industrial production, and energy consumption. Historical observations allow researchers to study the military capabilities of East and West Germany during the 1980s. Particularly relevant for evaluating Cold War military balances, defense preparedness, and the relative security capabilities of NATO and Warsaw Pact members.

returned_title: National Material Capabilities Data, 1816–1985 – ICPSR 9903
justification: Historical dataset archived by the Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research. Contains country-level indicators of military expenditure, military personnel, population, industrial production, and energy consumption. Includes the first half of the 1980s, making it useful for investigating military capabilities and security conditions in divided Germany. Particularly relevant for historical comparisons of East German and West German defense resources during the early Cold War escalation of the Reagan era.

returned_title: UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset (1946–2008)
justification: Historical armed-conflict dataset developed by the Uppsala Conflict Data Program and the Peace Research Institute Oslo. Covers interstate and internal armed conflicts over a period encompassing the entire 1980s. Relevant for examining Germany's broader international security environment, including conflicts involving NATO and Warsaw Pact countries. Although Germany itself was not experiencing conventional armed conflict during this decade, the dataset provides comparative evidence for studying the geopolitical conflict environment surrounding divided Germany.

returned_title: UCDP External Support Dataset (1975–2010)
justification: Dataset documenting external assistance provided to parties participating in intrastate armed conflicts. Covers the entire 1980s and identifies supporting actors, types of assistance, and years of involvement. Potentially relevant for investigating the international security activities of East and West Germany and their roles in Cold War conflicts abroad.
